questions.s: Which of the following is a pure substance?
questions.e: Distilled water contains only H₂O molecules, so it is a single compound and a pure substance. Air is a mixture of gases, brass is an alloy (a mixture of copper and zinc) and seawater contains many dissolved salts.

questions.s: Which process is a chemical change?
questions.e: Rusting forms a new substance, hydrated iron(III) oxide, so it is a chemical change. Melting, evaporation and dissolving only change the state or the arrangement of particles; the original substances can be recovered, so they are physical changes.

questions.s: Which of the following is a compound?
questions.e: Dry ice is carbon dioxide, which contains two different elements chemically combined, so it is a compound. Ozone and graphite contain only one element each (oxygen and carbon), so they are elements; stainless steel is an alloy, which is a mixture.

questions.s: When the equation aAl + bO₂ → cAl₂O₃ is balanced with the smallest whole numbers, what is a + b + c?
questions.e: Oxygen atoms: 2b = 3c, so take b = 3 and c = 2; then Al: a = 2c = 4. The balanced equation is 4Al + 3O₂ → 2Al₂O₃ and 4 + 3 + 2 = 9. A sum of 7 comes from the unbalanced guess 2Al + 3O₂ → 2Al₂O₃, which has 4 Al on the right but only 2 on the left.

questions.s: What is the formula of aluminium sulfate?
questions.e: Al³⁺ has a charge of +3 and SO₄²⁻ has a charge of −2; the lowest common multiple is 6, so 2 Al³⁺ balance 3 SO₄²⁻, giving Al₂(SO₄)₃. Al₃(SO₄)₂ swaps the numbers and would have a total charge of +9 − 4 = +5.

questions.s: Which test distinguishes a colloid from a true solution most easily?
o: Passing a beam of light through each liquid
Pouring each liquid through filter paper
Checking whether each liquid is transparent
Measuring the mass of each liquid
questions.e: A colloid scatters light and shows a bright path (the Tyndall effect); a true solution does not. Filtering does not work because colloid particles (1–100 nm) pass through filter paper just as solution particles do, and many colloids are transparent too.

questions.s: The reaction Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu belongs to which basic reaction type?
questions.e: An element (Zn) reacts with a compound (CuSO₄) to give a new element (Cu) and a new compound (ZnSO₄), which is a single displacement reaction. It is not double decomposition, because that type needs two compounds exchanging ions to form two new compounds.

questions.s: Which equation is correctly balanced?
questions.e: For 2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂: H is 4 = 4 and O is 4 = 2 + 2. The KClO₃ equation has 6 O on the left but only 4 on the right (it needs 3O₂), and the methane equation needs 2O₂ to supply the 4 O atoms on the right.

questions.s: Element X forms an oxide with the formula X₂O₃. If X has the same valency in its chloride, what is the formula of the chloride?
questions.e: In X₂O₃, 2 × (valency of X) = 3 × 2, so X has a valency of 3. Chlorine has a valency of 1, so the chloride is XCl₃. X₃Cl reverses the roles of the two elements.

questions.s: Metal Y has a valency of 2. What is the formula of its phosphate?
questions.e: Y²⁺ has charge +2 and PO₄³⁻ has charge −3; the lowest common multiple is 6, so 3 Y²⁺ balance 2 PO₄³⁻, giving Y₃(PO₄)₂. Y₂(PO₄)₃ would be correct only for a valency of 4.5, which is impossible; it comes from swapping the two numbers.

questions.s: What is the name of Na₂SO₃?
questions.e: The SO₃²⁻ ion is sulfite, so Na₂SO₃ is sodium sulfite. Sodium sulfate is Na₂SO₄ (one more oxygen), sodium sulfide is Na₂S and sodium thiosulfate is Na₂S₂O₃.

questions.s: Which list contains only mixtures?
questions.e: Air (several gases), brass (an alloy of Cu and Zn) and hydrochloric acid (HCl dissolved in water) are all mixtures. An ice-water mixture is pure H₂O in two states, ozone is an element and liquid nitrogen is pure N₂, so each of the other lists contains a pure substance.

questions.s: Which process involves only a physical change?
o: Burning magnesium ribbon in oxygen gas
Souring of milk left in a warm room
questions.e: Fractional distillation separates nitrogen, oxygen and argon by their boiling points; no new substance forms. Burning magnesium gives MgO, souring milk forms lactic acid and electrolysis splits water into H₂ and O₂, so these are all chemical changes.

questions.s: Pyrite is roasted in air: aFeS₂ + bO₂ → cFe₂O₃ + dSO₂. When balanced with the smallest whole numbers, what is b?
questions.e: Start with 2Fe₂O₃, which needs 4FeS₂ and therefore 8SO₂. Oxygen on the right is 2 × 3 + 8 × 2 = 22 atoms, so b = 11: 4FeS₂ + 11O₂ → 2Fe₂O₃ + 8SO₂. The value 8 is the coefficient of SO₂, not of O₂.

questions.s: The dispersed particles in a colloid have a diameter in which range?
questions.e: Colloids are defined by dispersed particles of 1–100 nm. Particles smaller than 1 nm form true solutions, and particles larger than about 100 nm form suspensions or emulsions, which settle or separate on standing.

questions.s: How is an iron(III) hydroxide colloid usually prepared in the laboratory?
o: Add NaOH solution to FeCl₃ solution and stir at room temperature
Heat solid FeCl₃ strongly in a crucible
Add FeCl₃ solution to cold water and filter
Add saturated FeCl₃ solution dropwise to boiling water
questions.e: Adding a few drops of saturated FeCl₃ solution to boiling water and heating until the liquid turns red-brown hydrolyses Fe³⁺ into tiny Fe(OH)₃ particles. Adding NaOH solution instead gives large particles that form a red-brown precipitate, not a colloid.

questions.s: Which reaction is a decomposition reaction?
o: CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ (adding water to lime)
questions.e: In a decomposition reaction one substance breaks down into two or more substances, as CaCO₃ does into CaO and CO₂. CaO + H₂O is a combination reaction, NaOH + HCl is a double decomposition (neutralisation) and Fe + HCl is a single displacement.

questions.s: Which statement about the three states of matter is correct?
o: Gases have neither a fixed shape nor a fixed volume
Gas particles are closer together than liquid particles
questions.e: Gas particles are far apart and move freely, so a gas fills any container and has no fixed shape or volume. Liquids take the shape of their container, solids are hardly compressible, and gas particles are much farther apart than liquid particles.

questions.s: What is the formula of calcium hydrogen carbonate?
questions.e: Ca²⁺ has charge +2 and the hydrogen carbonate ion HCO₃⁻ has charge −1, so two HCO₃⁻ ions are needed: Ca(HCO₃)₂. CaHCO₃ would leave an overall charge of +1.

questions.s: Propane burns completely: C₃H₈ + aO₂ → bCO₂ + cH₂O. When balanced with the smallest whole numbers, what is the sum of all the coefficients (including that of propane)?
questions.e: Carbon gives b = 3, hydrogen gives c = 4, and oxygen on the right is 3 × 2 + 4 = 10 atoms, so a = 5. The sum is 1 + 5 + 3 + 4 = 13. The answer 12 forgets to count the coefficient 1 of propane.

questions.s: Which pair of substances are allotropes of each other?
questions.e: Allotropes are different forms of the same element; O₂ and O₃ are both made only of oxygen. ¹²C and ¹⁴C are isotopes (atoms, not substances), while H₂O/H₂O₂ and CO/CO₂ are different compounds.

questions.s: Which of the following is a basic oxide?
questions.e: MgO reacts with acids to give a salt and water (MgO + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂O), so it is a basic oxide. CO₂ and SO₃ are acidic oxides that react with bases, and CO is a neutral oxide that reacts with neither.

questions.s: Which notation represents two nitrogen molecules?
questions.e: Nitrogen exists as N₂ molecules, and the coefficient 2 in front means two of them: 2N₂. 2N means two nitrogen atoms, and N₂ alone means one molecule.

questions.s: Copper reacts with dilute nitric acid: 3Cu + 8HNO₃ → 3Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2X + 4H₂O. What is X?
questions.e: Atoms are conserved. N: 8 on the left and 6 in 3Cu(NO₃)₂, so 2X contain 2 N. O: 24 on the left, 18 + 4 = 22 on the right without X, so 2X contain 2 O. Hence X = NO. NO₂ is produced by concentrated nitric acid, not dilute.

questions.s: A sample is known to contain only one element. Which conclusion is correct?
o: It must be an element, as only one element is present
It must be a pure substance with a fixed composition
It may be either a pure substance or a mixture
questions.e: A sample with one element can be a single element (pure O₂) or a mixture of allotropes (O₂ mixed with O₃, or diamond mixed with graphite). So it is not necessarily pure, and it can never be a compound, which needs at least two elements.

questions.s: What is the formula of ammonium nitrate?
questions.e: The ammonium ion NH₄⁺ (charge +1) combines with the nitrate ion NO₃⁻ (charge −1) in a 1 : 1 ratio, giving NH₄NO₃. NH₃NO₃ uses ammonia, a neutral molecule, instead of the ammonium ion.

questions.s: When 12 g of magnesium burns completely in oxygen, 20 g of magnesium oxide forms. What mass of oxygen reacted?
questions.e: By conservation of mass, mass of O₂ = mass of MgO − mass of Mg = 20 g − 12 g = 8 g. 32 g is the molar mass of O₂, not the mass that reacted here.

questions.s: In the catalytic oxidation of ammonia, aNH₃ + bO₂ → cNO + dH₂O. When balanced with the smallest whole numbers, what is b?
questions.e: Balance H first: 2NH₃ gives 3H₂O, so use 4NH₃ → 4NO + 6H₂O. Oxygen on the right is 4 + 6 = 10 atoms, so b = 5: 4NH₃ + 5O₂ → 4NO + 6H₂O. The value 6 is the coefficient of water.

questions.s: Which statement about oxides is correct?
o: All metal oxides are basic oxides
All non-metal oxides are acidic oxides
Na₂O₂ is a basic oxide because it reacts with water to form NaOH
SiO₂ is an acidic oxide although it does not dissolve in water
questions.e: SiO₂ reacts with bases (SiO₂ + 2NaOH → Na₂SiO₃ + H₂O), so it is an acidic oxide even though it is insoluble in water. Some metal oxides are not basic (Al₂O₃ is amphoteric, Mn₂O₇ is acidic), CO and NO are neutral non-metal oxides, and Na₂O₂ is a peroxide that gives O₂ as well as NaOH with water.

questions.s: Which of the following is a physical property of a substance?
questions.e: Boiling point can be measured without changing the substance into a new one, so it is a physical property. Flammability, reactivity with acids and rusting can only be observed through chemical reactions, so they are chemical properties.

questions.s: Which reaction is a double decomposition reaction?
questions.e: Two compounds exchange their ions (Ba²⁺ pairs with SO₄²⁻ and Na⁺ with Cl⁻) to give two new compounds, which is double decomposition; it goes to completion because BaSO₄ precipitates. The others are combination, single displacement and decomposition reactions.

questions.s: Which reaction is a combination reaction and also a redox reaction?
questions.e: Two substances form one product, and Fe changes from +2 to +3 while Cl changes from 0 to −1, so it is a redox combination reaction. CaO + H₂O is a combination reaction but no oxidation state changes, so it is not redox.

questions.s: Which of the following is a colloid?
questions.e: Fog consists of tiny water droplets (about 1–100 nm) dispersed in air, so it is a colloid and shows the Tyndall effect. Salt water and CuSO₄ solution are true solutions, and muddy water is a suspension whose particles settle.

questions.s: Tofu is made by adding a little brine (containing MgCl₂) to hot soy milk, which then sets. Which property of colloids does this use?
o: Coagulation of a colloid by an electrolyte
Neutralisation of an acid in the soy milk by a base in the brine
questions.e: Soy milk is a protein colloid. Ions from the added electrolyte neutralise the charges on the colloid particles, so they clump together and coagulate. The Tyndall effect is light scattering and plays no part in setting the tofu.

questions.s: A starch colloid contains some dissolved NaCl. Which method removes the Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions while keeping the starch particles?
o: Filtration through ordinary filter paper several times
questions.e: Small ions pass through a semi-permeable membrane but colloid particles (1–100 nm) do not, so dialysis separates them. Filter paper lets both the ions and the colloid particles pass, so filtration cannot separate them.

questions.s: Element R forms an oxide R₂O₃ whose relative formula mass is 102. What is the relative atomic mass of R? (O = 16)
questions.e: 2 × Ar(R) + 3 × 16 = 102, so 2 × Ar(R) = 54 and Ar(R) = 27 (aluminium). The value 54 forgets to divide by the 2 atoms of R in the formula.

questions.s: Which formula is written incorrectly?
questions.e: K⁺ has charge +1 and SO₄²⁻ has charge −2, so two K⁺ are needed: the correct formula is K₂SO₄. In the other formulas the charges balance: Mg²⁺ with 2Cl⁻, 2Na⁺ with CO₃²⁻, and 2Fe³⁺ with 3SO₄²⁻.

questions.s: What is the systematic name of FeSO₄?
questions.e: SO₄²⁻ is sulfate with charge −2, so the single iron ion must be Fe²⁺: iron(II) sulfate (ferrous sulfate). Iron(III) sulfate is Fe₂(SO₄)₃, and sulfite would be SO₃²⁻.

questions.s: How many atoms in total are in one formula unit of copper(II) sulfate pentahydrate, CuSO₄·5H₂O?
questions.e: CuSO₄ has 1 + 1 + 4 = 6 atoms and 5H₂O has 5 × 3 = 15 atoms, so the total is 21. The answer 11 counts the water molecules as 5 atoms instead of 15.

questions.s: Consider: burning paper, dissolving salt in water, digesting food, crushing an aluminium can, baking a cake. How many of these are chemical changes?
questions.e: Burning paper, digesting food and baking a cake all form new substances, so there are 3 chemical changes. Dissolving salt and crushing a can change only the form or arrangement of particles, so they are physical changes.

questions.s: Copper reacts with concentrated nitric acid: aCu + bHNO₃ → cCu(NO₃)₂ + dNO₂ + eH₂O. When balanced with the smallest whole numbers, what is b?
questions.e: Cu loses 2 electrons and each N going from +5 to +4 gains 1, so 1 Cu gives 2NO₂. Nitrogen: 2 in Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2 in NO₂ = 4, so b = 4 and e = 2: Cu + 4HNO₃ → Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2NO₂ + 2H₂O. The value 8 belongs to the reaction with dilute acid, which gives NO.

questions.s: Which statement about blue copper(II) sulfate pentahydrate, CuSO₄·5H₂O, is correct?
o: It is a mixture of CuSO₄ and water
It is a compound and therefore a pure substance
Turning it into white CuSO₄ by heating is a physical change
It is an element because it has a fixed formula
questions.e: CuSO₄·5H₂O has a fixed composition, so it is a single compound, a pure substance. Heating removes the water of crystallisation and forms a new substance (white anhydrous CuSO₄), which is a chemical change.

questions.s: In the expression 3H₂SO₄, what does the number 3 show?
o: Three hydrogen atoms in one molecule
Three sulfur atoms in one molecule
questions.e: A coefficient in front of a formula gives the number of molecules (or formula units), so 3H₂SO₄ means three sulfuric acid molecules. The number of atoms inside one molecule is shown by subscripts, such as the 2 in H₂.

questions.s: Which change is sublimation?
o: Water vapour condensing into liquid droplets on a cold window
Frost forming directly from water vapour
Solid iodine turning into violet vapour on gentle heating
questions.e: Sublimation is a change directly from solid to gas, as when iodine crystals give violet vapour. Frost forming from vapour is the reverse change (gas to solid, called deposition), and condensation is gas to liquid.

questions.s: Which change of state releases energy to the surroundings?
questions.e: When steam condenses, particles come closer and attractive forces form, so energy is released (which is why steam burns are severe). Melting, evaporation and sublimation all need energy to separate the particles, so they absorb heat.

questions.s: Which basic type of reaction is Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂?
questions.e: Two compounds exchange ions to give new compounds (the H₂CO₃ formed breaks down into H₂O and CO₂), so it is a double decomposition reaction. It is not a single displacement because no free element reacts or forms.

questions.s: An oxide of nitrogen contains nitrogen and oxygen in the mass ratio 7 : 16. What is its formula? (N = 14, O = 16)
questions.e: Mole ratio N : O = 7/14 : 16/16 = 0.5 : 1 = 1 : 2, so the formula is NO₂. Treating the mass ratio 7 : 16 as an atom ratio (about 1 : 2.3) might suggest N₂O₅, but atoms must be compared in moles, not grams.

questions.s: In an electrophoresis experiment, the red-brown Fe(OH)₃ colloid particles move towards the cathode. Which conclusion is correct?
o: The whole colloid is positively charged
The colloid particles must be negatively charged
The colloid particles carry a positive charge
The movement is caused by the Tyndall effect
questions.e: Particles moving to the negative electrode must carry positive charge; Fe(OH)₃ particles adsorb Fe³⁺ ions. The colloid as a whole is still electrically neutral because the surrounding liquid contains an equal amount of negative charge.

questions.s: Which of the following is an amphoteric oxide?
questions.e: Al₂O₃ reacts with acids (giving Al³⁺ salts) and with strong bases (giving aluminates such as NaAlO₂), so it is amphoteric. Na₂O and CaO react only with acids (basic oxides), and SO₂ reacts only with bases (acidic oxide).

questions.s: Which substance is a binary compound (made of exactly two elements)?
questions.e: CaCl₂ contains only calcium and chlorine. KClO₃ (K, Cl, O), NaOH (Na, O, H) and H₂SO₄ (H, S, O) each contain three elements.

questions.s: Potassium permanganate decomposes on heating: aKMnO₄ → bK₂MnO₄ + cMnO₂ + dO₂. When balanced with the smallest whole numbers, what is a + b + c + d?
questions.e: K atoms force a = 2b; with b = 1 we get a = 2, c = 1 (Mn: 2 = 1 + 1) and oxygen 8 = 4 + 2 + 2d gives d = 1. So 2KMnO₄ → K₂MnO₄ + MnO₂ + O₂ and the sum is 5. The sum 4 comes from leaving every coefficient as 1, which leaves K and Mn unbalanced.

questions.s: In a thermite-type reaction, aFe₃O₄ + bAl → cAl₂O₃ + dFe. When balanced with the smallest whole numbers, what is b?
questions.e: Oxygen: 4a = 3c, so a = 3 and c = 4. Then Al: b = 2c = 8 and Fe: d = 3a = 9, giving 3Fe₃O₄ + 8Al → 4Al₂O₃ + 9Fe. The value 9 is the coefficient of iron, not of aluminium.

questions.s: Sodium hydrogen carbonate decomposes on heating: 2NaHCO₃ → Na₂CO₃ + X + CO₂. What is X?
questions.e: Left side: 2 Na, 2 H, 2 C, 6 O. Right side without X: 2 Na, 2 C, 5 O. So X contains 2 H and 1 O, which is H₂O. H₂ would leave one O atom unaccounted for.

questions.s: A pure compound melts sharply at a fixed temperature. A student's sample of a white solid melts gradually between 76 °C and 80 °C. What is the best conclusion?
o: It is certainly a pure compound
questions.e: Pure substances have a sharp, fixed melting point; impurities lower the melting point and spread it over a range. A melting range of 4 °C therefore suggests a mixture. Elements are pure substances too, so they would also melt sharply.

questions.s: The formula of calcium phosphate is Ca₃(PO₄)₂. What is the valency of the phosphate group?
questions.e: Calcium has a valency of 2, so the total for 3 Ca is 6. This must equal 2 × (valency of PO₄), so the phosphate group has a valency of 3 (PO₄³⁻). Reading the subscript 2 as the valency gives the wrong answer.

questions.s: Metal M forms a sulfate with the formula M₂(SO₄)₃. What is the formula of its nitrate?
questions.e: Three SO₄²⁻ carry −6, shared by 2 M, so M is M³⁺. Each nitrate ion is NO₃⁻, so three are needed: M(NO₃)₃. M₂(NO₃)₃ copies the 2 from the sulfate formula and leaves a total charge of +3.

questions.s: What is the name of the acid HClO?
questions.e: Chlorine oxoacids are named by oxygen count: HClO hypochlorous, HClO₂ chlorous, HClO₃ chloric, HClO₄ perchloric. Hydrochloric acid is HCl, which contains no oxygen.

questions.s: Which acid is diprotic, that is, one molecule can release two H⁺ ions?
questions.e: H₂SO₄ ionises in two steps, giving up to 2 H⁺ per molecule. Acetic acid contains four H atoms, but only the H of the –COOH group ionises, so it is monoprotic; H₃PO₄ is triprotic.

questions.s: Which compound is an alkali (a base that is soluble in water)?
questions.e: KOH is a base and dissolves readily in water, so it is an alkali. Cu(OH)₂ and Fe(OH)₃ are bases but are insoluble; Na₂CO₃ gives an alkaline solution but it is a salt, not a base.

questions.s: How is sodium hydrogen carbonate, NaHCO₃, classified?
questions.e: NaHCO₃ is a salt whose anion still contains a replaceable hydrogen from the parent acid H₂CO₃, so it is an acid salt. Its solution is weakly alkaline, but that does not make it a base; it is formed from an acid and a base like any salt.

questions.s: Which reaction is a decomposition reaction that is also a redox reaction?
questions.e: In 2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂, oxygen changes from −1 to −2 and to 0, so oxidation states change. The other three are decompositions in which every element keeps its oxidation state, so they are not redox reactions.

questions.s: Which statement about the basic reaction types is correct?
o: Every combination reaction is a redox reaction
Every single displacement reaction is a redox reaction
Every decomposition reaction is a redox reaction
Some double decomposition reactions are redox reactions
questions.e: In a single displacement an element becomes part of a compound and another element is released, so oxidation states must change. Combination and decomposition reactions may or may not be redox (CaO + H₂O and CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ are not), and double decomposition reactions only exchange ions, so they are never redox.

questions.s: Alum, KAl(SO₄)₂·12H₂O, is used to clarify muddy water. How does it work?
o: Al³⁺ forms an Al(OH)₃ colloid that adsorbs suspended particles, which settle
Alum oxidises and kills the bacteria in the water
Alum reacts with the mud to form a soluble salt
Alum raises the boiling point so the mud stays behind
questions.e: Al³⁺ hydrolyses in water to give an Al(OH)₃ colloid with a large surface area; it adsorbs fine suspended particles, which then settle out. Alum is not an oxidising agent, so it does not disinfect the water; that needs chlorine or similar.

questions.s: Which everyday observation is an example of the Tyndall effect?
o: Bright beams of sunlight in a misty forest
Salt disappearing as it dissolves in soup
The blue colour of copper(II) sulfate solution
questions.e: Mist is a colloid; its droplets scatter sunlight so the path of the light becomes visible, which is the Tyndall effect. A rainbow is caused by refraction and dispersion of light in raindrops, not by scattering in a colloid.

questions.s: What is the essential difference between a colloid and a solution?
o: The size of the dispersed particles
Whether it passes through filter paper
Whether it separates into layers quickly
questions.e: Colloid particles are 1–100 nm across while solution particles are below 1 nm; every other difference follows from this. Both pass through filter paper, both can be coloured or colourless, and colloids are fairly stable rather than separating quickly.

questions.s: A gas in a syringe is compressed at constant temperature. What decreases?
o: The average distance between the particles
questions.e: Compressing a gas pushes the particles closer together, so only the spaces between them shrink. The particles themselves keep the same size and mass, and no particles are lost from the sealed syringe.

questions.s: Cotton wool soaked in concentrated ammonia solution is placed at one end of a long glass tube, and cotton wool soaked in concentrated hydrochloric acid at the other end. A white ring of NH₄Cl forms inside the tube. Where does it form, and why?
o: Nearer the HCl end, because NH₃ molecules are lighter and diffuse faster
Nearer the NH₃ end, because NH₃ molecules are lighter and diffuse faster
Exactly in the middle, because both gases diffuse at the same rate
Nearer the HCl end, because HCl molecules are lighter and diffuse faster
questions.e: NH₃ (Mr = 17) is lighter than HCl (Mr = 36.5), so it diffuses faster and travels further before the two gases meet; the ring forms nearer the HCl end. Placing the ring near the NH₃ end would mean the slower gas travelled further, which contradicts the reasoning.

questions.s: Ethanol burns completely: C₂H₅OH + aO₂ → bCO₂ + cH₂O. When balanced with the smallest whole numbers, what is a?
questions.e: Carbon gives b = 2 and hydrogen (6 atoms) gives c = 3. Oxygen on the right is 4 + 3 = 7; ethanol already supplies 1 O, so O₂ supplies 6 atoms and a = 3. The answer 6 counts oxygen atoms instead of O₂ molecules.

questions.s: For the equation 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, which statement is correct?
o: 2 molecules of H₂ react with 1 molecule of O₂ to form 2 molecules of H₂O
2 g of H₂ reacts with 1 g of O₂ to form 2 g of H₂O
The total number of molecules is the same before and after
H₂ and O₂ react in a mole ratio of 1 : 8 to form water
questions.e: Coefficients give ratios of molecules or moles, so 2 H₂ molecules react with 1 O₂ molecule. The mass ratio is 4 g : 32 g = 1 : 8, which is not the mole ratio, and the number of molecules falls from 3 to 2, although atoms and mass are conserved.

questions.s: A compound X burns: X + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O. What is the formula of X?
questions.e: Right side: 2 C, 6 H and 4 + 3 = 7 O. Left side without X: 6 O. So X contains 2 C, 6 H and 1 O, which is C₂H₆O (for example ethanol). C₂H₆ would need 3.5 O₂ per molecule, not 3.

questions.s: What is the formula of the permanganate ion in potassium permanganate, KMnO₄?
questions.e: One K⁺ balances the anion, so the permanganate ion is MnO₄⁻. MnO₄²⁻ is the manganate ion found in K₂MnO₄, which needs two K⁺ ions.

questions.s: Which name and formula are correctly matched?
questions.e: HSO₄⁻ has charge −1, so one Na⁺ gives NaHSO₄. Potassium chlorate is KClO₃ (KCl is potassium chloride), calcium hydroxide is Ca(OH)₂ and ammonium sulfate is (NH₄)₂SO₄.

questions.s: Which pair lists an element followed by a compound?
questions.e: Mercury is an element and sodium chloride is a compound of Na and Cl. Steel and air are mixtures, and ozone and oxygen are both elements (allotropes).

questions.s: Which of the following changes is a chemical change?
o: Ice melting on a warm day
White anhydrous CuSO₄ turning blue when water is added
Dry ice turning directly into gas
questions.e: Anhydrous CuSO₄ combines with water to form a new compound, blue CuSO₄·5H₂O, so this is a chemical change. A glowing filament gives out light and heat but stays tungsten, so it is a physical change.

questions.s: Which statement about physical and chemical changes is correct?
o: Giving out heat and light does not prove a chemical change
Every change of state is a chemical change
A change in which a gas is given off must always be a chemical change
A change with no visible sign can never be a chemical change
questions.e: An electric lamp gives out heat and light with no new substance formed, so these signs alone do not prove a chemical change. Boiling water gives off a gas but is physical, and some chemical changes (such as many neutralisations) show no visible sign.

questions.s: Glucose is oxidised in respiration: C₆H₁₂O₆ + bO₂ → cCO₂ + dH₂O. When balanced with the smallest whole numbers, what is b?
questions.e: Carbon gives c = 6 and hydrogen gives d = 6. Oxygen on the right is 12 + 6 = 18; glucose supplies 6, so O₂ supplies 12 atoms and b = 6. The answer 12 counts oxygen atoms rather than O₂ molecules.

questions.s: Chlorine is made from manganese dioxide and concentrated hydrochloric acid: aMnO₂ + bHCl → cMnCl₂ + dCl₂ + eH₂O. When balanced with the smallest whole numbers, what is b?
questions.e: Mn goes from +4 to +2 (gains 2e⁻), and 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ loses 2e⁻, so a = c = d = 1. Chlorine: 2 in MnCl₂ + 2 in Cl₂ = 4, so b = 4 and e = 2: MnO₂ + 4HCl → MnCl₂ + Cl₂ + 2H₂O. The answer 2 counts only the HCl that is oxidised.

questions.s: Sodium peroxide reacts with carbon dioxide: aNa₂O₂ + bCO₂ → cNa₂CO₃ + dO₂. When balanced with the smallest whole numbers, what is a + b + c + d?
questions.e: Na and C give a = c and b = c. Oxygen: 2a + 2b = 3c + 2d; with a = b = c = 2 this gives 8 = 6 + 2d, so d = 1. Thus 2Na₂O₂ + 2CO₂ → 2Na₂CO₃ + O₂ and the sum is 7. Writing every coefficient as 1 gives 4, but then oxygen is 4 on the left and 5 on the right.

questions.s: Which of the following is caused by the coagulation of a colloid?
o: A delta forming where a muddy river meets the sea
Fresh water obtained by distilling seawater
Ice melting faster when salt is sprinkled on it
Sand removed from water by filtration
questions.e: River water carries charged clay colloid particles; the salts in seawater neutralise their charge, so they coagulate and settle, building a delta. Distillation, filtration and the effect of salt on ice do not involve colloids.

questions.s: Which halogen is a liquid at 25 °C and normal atmospheric pressure?
questions.e: Bromine is a red-brown liquid at room temperature. Fluorine and chlorine are gases and iodine is a dark grey solid, because intermolecular forces increase down the group.

questions.s: Which of the following is a mixture?
questions.e: Milk contains water, fats, proteins, sugars and minerals in variable amounts, so it is a mixture. Sodium chloride and glucose are compounds and copper is an element; all three are pure substances.

questions.s: While a candle burns, which process is a chemical change?
o: Wax vapour burning to form CO₂ and H₂O
Molten wax setting on the side of the candle
Wax softening in a warm room
questions.e: Burning wax vapour produces new substances, carbon dioxide and water, so it is a chemical change. Melting, setting and softening only change the state of the wax, which is still wax afterwards.

questions.s: What is the formula of magnesium nitrate?
questions.e: Mg²⁺ has charge +2 and NO₃⁻ has charge −1, so two nitrate ions are needed: Mg(NO₃)₂. MgNO₃ would leave an overall charge of +1.

questions.s: Iron burns in chlorine: aFe + bCl₂ → cFeCl₃. When balanced with the smallest whole numbers, what is b?
questions.e: Chlorine: 2b = 3c, so the smallest choice is b = 3 and c = 2, then a = 2: 2Fe + 3Cl₂ → 2FeCl₃. The value 6 is the number of chlorine atoms, not the number of Cl₂ molecules.

questions.s: What is the name of KClO₃?
questions.e: ClO₃⁻ is the chlorate ion, so KClO₃ is potassium chlorate. Chlorite is ClO₂⁻, perchlorate is ClO₄⁻ and potassium chloride is KCl with no oxygen.

questions.s: How is the reaction 2HgO → 2Hg + O₂ (on heating) best described?
o: A combination reaction that is also a redox reaction
A decomposition reaction that is not a redox reaction
A decomposition reaction that is also a redox reaction
questions.e: One compound breaks into two substances, so it is a decomposition. Mercury goes from +2 to 0 and oxygen from −2 to 0, so oxidation states change and it is also a redox reaction. Any reaction that produces a free element from a compound like this involves electron transfer.

questions.s: A torch beam is shone through four liquids in a dark room. In which liquid is a bright path of light seen?
questions.e: Starch molecules are large enough (1–100 nm) to form a colloid, which scatters light and shows the Tyndall effect. The other three are true solutions whose particles are too small to scatter light visibly, even when coloured like CuSO₄ solution.

questions.s: Element X has a valency of 3 and element Y has a valency of 2. What is the formula of the compound they form?
questions.e: The total valency must match: 2 × 3 = 3 × 2 = 6, so two X atoms combine with three Y atoms, giving X₂Y₃. X₃Y₂ swaps the numbers and gives 9 on one side and 4 on the other.

questions.s: Ethene burns completely: aC₂H₄ + bO₂ → cCO₂ + dH₂O. When balanced with the smallest whole numbers, what is a + b + c + d?
questions.e: With a = 1: carbon gives c = 2, hydrogen gives d = 2, and oxygen on the right is 4 + 2 = 6 atoms, so b = 3. The sum is 1 + 3 + 2 + 2 = 8. The answer 7 forgets the coefficient 1 of ethene.

questions.s: 10 g of calcium carbonate is heated until it has completely decomposed, leaving 5.6 g of calcium oxide. What mass of carbon dioxide was given off?
questions.e: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂; by conservation of mass, mass of CO₂ = 10 g − 5.6 g = 4.4 g. Adding the masses (15.6 g) wrongly treats the CaO as a second reactant.

questions.s: Which pair of changes are both physical changes?
o: Distilling seawater; dissolving iodine in ethanol
Rusting iron; bending a copper wire
questions.e: Distillation and dissolving only separate or mix substances without forming new ones. Each other pair contains one chemical change: burning coal, fermentation and rusting all form new substances.

questions.s: An oxide is a compound of exactly two elements, one of which is oxygen. Which substance is an oxide?
questions.e: Al₂O₃ contains only aluminium and oxygen, so it is an oxide. KClO₃, Ca(OH)₂ and H₂SO₄ contain oxygen but each has three elements, so they are a salt, a base and an acid respectively.

questions.s: Which substance is a base?
questions.e: Mg(OH)₂ consists of a metal ion and hydroxide ions only, and it neutralises acids to give a salt and water, so it is a base. Na₂CO₃ is a salt (its solution is alkaline), Cu₂(OH)₂CO₃ is a basic salt and ethanol's –OH group does not ionise, so ethanol is not a base.

questions.s: Calcium carbide reacts with water: CaC₂ + 2H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + X. What is X?
questions.e: Left side: 1 Ca, 2 C, 4 H, 2 O. Ca(OH)₂ takes 1 Ca, 2 O and 2 H, leaving 2 C and 2 H, so X is C₂H₂ (ethyne). C₂H₄ would need 4 H atoms left over, but only 2 remain.

questions.s: On a very cold night, water vapour in the air turns directly into ice crystals on a window. What is this change called?
questions.e: A change directly from gas to solid is deposition (sometimes called desublimation). Sublimation is the opposite change, solid to gas, and condensation and freezing each involve a liquid.

questions.s: In which dispersion are the dispersed particles between 1 nm and 100 nm in size?
questions.e: A colloid by definition has particles of 1–100 nm. FeCl₃ solution has ions smaller than 1 nm, while a stirred precipitate (a suspension) and oil shaken with water (an emulsion) contain particles larger than 100 nm that settle or separate.

questions.s: How are diamond and graphite related?
questions.e: Diamond and graphite are different forms of the element carbon with different structures, so they are allotropes. Isotopes are atoms of one element with different neutron numbers, and isomers are compounds with the same molecular formula.

questions.s: What is the systematic name of Fe₂O₃?
questions.e: Three O²⁻ ions carry −6, shared by 2 Fe, so each iron is +3: iron(III) oxide. Iron(II) oxide is FeO and iron(II,III) oxide is Fe₃O₄.

questions.s: Aluminium reacts with dilute sulfuric acid: aAl + bH₂SO₄ → cAl₂(SO₄)₃ + dH₂. When balanced with the smallest whole numbers, what is a + b + c + d?
questions.e: With c = 1: Al gives a = 2, sulfate gives b = 3, and hydrogen gives d = 3. So 2Al + 3H₂SO₄ → Al₂(SO₄)₃ + 3H₂ and the sum is 2 + 3 + 1 + 3 = 9. Forgetting the coefficient 1 of Al₂(SO₄)₃ gives 8.

questions.s: Which reaction is a combination reaction?
questions.e: In a combination reaction two or more substances form a single product, as sulfur and oxygen form SO₂. The others are a decomposition, a single displacement and a double decomposition (neutralisation).

questions.s: How many oxygen atoms are there in 2Al₂(SO₄)₃?
questions.e: One formula unit has 3 sulfate groups × 4 O = 12 oxygen atoms, and the coefficient 2 doubles this to 24. The answer 12 forgets the coefficient, and 14 ignores the bracket (2 × (4 + 3)).

questions.s: Which statement is correct?
o: Liquid oxygen is a mixture of oxygen and air
Crystalline hydrates such as CuSO₄·5H₂O are mixtures
Pure water is an element because it has one formula
questions.e: Hydrochloric acid is hydrogen chloride dissolved in water, so it is a mixture (a solution). Liquid oxygen is pure O₂, a hydrate has a fixed composition and is a compound, and water contains two elements, so it is a compound.

questions.s: What is the mass ratio of carbon to hydrogen in methane, CH₄? (C = 12, H = 1)
questions.e: Mass of C : mass of H = 12 : (4 × 1) = 12 : 4 = 3 : 1. The ratio 1 : 4 is the ratio of atoms, not of masses, and 12 : 1 forgets that there are four H atoms.

questions.s: How do the particles in a solid behave?
o: They move freely through the whole container
They are far apart from one another
They do not move at all
questions.e: Particles in a solid are closely packed and held in fixed positions, but they still vibrate, and vibrate more as the temperature rises. Moving freely and being far apart describe a gas.

questions.s: Ammonia burns in pure oxygen: 4NH₃ + 3O₂ → 2X + 6H₂O. What is X?
questions.e: Left side: 4 N, 12 H, 6 O. 6H₂O contains 12 H and 6 O, so 2X contain only the 4 N atoms and X = N₂. NO is the product of catalytic oxidation (4NH₃ + 5O₂ → 4NO + 6H₂O), which uses more oxygen.

questions.s: What is the relative molecular mass of sulfuric acid, H₂SO₄? (H = 1, S = 32, O = 16)
questions.e: Mr = 2(1) + 32 + 4(16) = 2 + 32 + 64 = 98. The value 82 counts only three oxygen atoms, 96 leaves out the two hydrogen atoms, and 49 is half the correct value.

questions.s: What is the relative formula mass of calcium carbonate, CaCO₃? (C = 12, O = 16, Ca = 40)
questions.e: Mr = 40 + 12 + 3(16) = 100. The value 68 uses only one oxygen atom, 88 forgets the carbon atom, and 116 uses four oxygen atoms instead of three.

questions.s: What is the relative formula mass of aluminium sulfate, Al₂(SO₄)₃? (O = 16, Al = 27, S = 32)
questions.e: One SO₄ group has mass 32 + 64 = 96, so Mr = 2(27) + 3(96) = 54 + 288 = 342. The value 214 applies the subscript 3 to sulfur only, and 150 ignores the subscript outside the bracket altogether.

questions.s: What is the molar mass of copper(II) sulfate pentahydrate, CuSO₄·5H₂O? (H = 1, O = 16, S = 32, Cu = 64)
questions.e: CuSO₄ = 64 + 32 + 64 = 160 and 5H₂O = 5 × 18 = 90, so M = 160 + 90 = 250 g/mol. 160 g/mol ignores the water of crystallisation and 178 g/mol counts only one water molecule.

questions.s: Which statement about the mole is correct?
o: One mole of every substance has a mass of exactly 12 g
One mole contains as many particles as there are atoms in 12 g of carbon-12
One mole of any gas occupies 22.4 L at any temperature and pressure
The mole is the SI unit used for the mass of particles
questions.e: The mole is the amount of substance containing as many particles as there are atoms in 12 g of carbon-12 (about 6.02 × 10²³). The mass of one mole depends on the substance, and 22.4 L/mol applies to gases only at STP (0 °C, 101 kPa). The mole measures amount of substance, not mass.

questions.s: How many molecules are present in 0.5 mol of water? (Take NA = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹)
questions.e: N = n × NA = 0.5 × 6.02 × 10²³ = 3.01 × 10²³ molecules. 9.03 × 10²³ is the number of atoms (three per molecule), not molecules.

questions.s: How many atoms in total are present in 0.2 mol of ammonia, NH₃? (NA is the Avogadro constant)
questions.e: Each NH₃ molecule has 1 N + 3 H = 4 atoms, so n(atoms) = 0.2 × 4 = 0.8 mol, i.e. 0.8 NA atoms. 0.6 NA counts only the hydrogen atoms and 0.2 NA counts molecules.

questions.s: How many hydrogen atoms are present in 9 g of water? (H = 1, O = 16; NA = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹)
questions.e: n(H₂O) = 9/18 = 0.5 mol, and each molecule has 2 H atoms, so n(H) = 1 mol = 6.02 × 10²³ atoms. 3.01 × 10²³ is the number of water molecules, and 9.03 × 10²³ is the total number of atoms.

questions.s: What is the mass of 0.25 mol of sodium hydroxide, NaOH? (H = 1, O = 16, Na = 23)
questions.e: M(NaOH) = 23 + 16 + 1 = 40 g/mol, so m = nM = 0.25 × 40 = 10 g. 160 g comes from dividing 40 by 0.25 instead of multiplying, and 0.00625 g from dividing 0.25 by 40.

questions.s: What amount of substance is present in 4.4 g of carbon dioxide? (C = 12, O = 16)
questions.e: M(CO₂) = 12 + 32 = 44 g/mol, so n = m/M = 4.4/44 = 0.1 mol. 10 mol comes from the inverted ratio 44/4.4, and 0.2 mol from using half the molar mass.

questions.s: Which sample contains the greatest number of molecules? (H = 1, C = 12, N = 14, O = 16)
questions.e: Number of molecules is proportional to n = m/M: CO₂ 44/44 = 1 mol, O₂ 32/32 = 1 mol, NH₃ 17/17 = 1 mol, H₂ 4/2 = 2 mol. The largest mass (CO₂) does not mean the most molecules, because its molar mass is also large.

questions.s: What is the mass of a single water molecule? (H = 1, O = 16; take NA = 6.0 × 10²³ mol⁻¹)
questions.e: One mole (18 g) contains 6.0 × 10²³ molecules, so one molecule has mass 18/(6.0 × 10²³) = 3.0 × 10⁻²³ g. Multiplying 18 by NA (1.08 × 10²⁵ g) or dividing NA by 18 gives absurd masses for one molecule.

questions.s: 0.25 mol of a gas X has a mass of 16 g. Which could X be? (C = 12, N = 14, O = 16, S = 32)
questions.e: M = m/n = 16/0.25 = 64 g/mol, which matches SO₂ (32 + 32 = 64). O₂ (32) would fit only if the amount were 0.5 mol; CO₂ is 44 and NO₂ is 46.

questions.s: Equal masses of oxygen, O₂, and ozone, O₃, are compared. Which statement is correct? (O = 16)
o: The ratio of their numbers of molecules is 1 : 1
The ratio of their numbers of molecules is 2 : 3
The ratio of their numbers of oxygen atoms is 1 : 1
The ratio of their numbers of oxygen atoms is 2 : 3
questions.e: Both are made only of oxygen atoms, so equal masses contain equal numbers of O atoms (m/16 mol each). The molecule ratio is (m/32) : (m/48) = 3 : 2, so 2 : 3 is the inverse of the true molecule ratio.

questions.s: a g of ammonia, NH₃, contains b hydrogen atoms. Which expression gives the Avogadro constant? (H = 1, N = 14)
questions.e: n(NH₃) = a/17 mol, so n(H) = 3a/17 mol. NA = number of atoms / amount = b ÷ (3a/17) = 17b/(3a) mol⁻¹. 17b/a forgets that each molecule has three H atoms, and 51b/a multiplies by 3 instead of dividing.

questions.s: The relative atomic mass of an element is the average mass of its atoms compared with which quantity?
o: 1/12 of the mass of a carbon-12 atom
the mass of one hydrogen atom
the mass of one carbon-12 atom
1/16 of the mass of an oxygen-16 atom
questions.e: Relative atomic masses are measured against 1/12 of the mass of one carbon-12 atom, which makes Ar(C-12) exactly 12. Comparing with a whole carbon-12 atom would give carbon a value of 1; the hydrogen and oxygen standards are historical, not the current definition.

questions.s: Chlorine consists of the isotopes ³⁵Cl and ³⁷Cl, and its relative atomic mass is 35.5. What percentage of chlorine atoms are ³⁵Cl?
questions.e: Let the fraction of ³⁵Cl be x: 35x + 37(1 − x) = 35.5, so 37 − 2x = 35.5 and x = 0.75, i.e. 75 %. 25 % is the share of ³⁷Cl, and 50 % would give an average of 36.

questions.s: Natural boron contains ¹⁰B and ¹¹B, and its relative atomic mass is 10.8. What is the ratio of the number of ¹⁰B atoms to ¹¹B atoms?
questions.e: If x is the fraction of ¹⁰B: 10x + 11(1 − x) = 10.8, so x = 0.2. Then ¹⁰B : ¹¹B = 0.2 : 0.8 = 1 : 4. The ratio 4 : 1 swaps the isotopes; an average of 10.8 is closer to 11, so ¹¹B must be the more common one.

questions.s: At STP, 2.24 L of a gas has a mass of 2.8 g. Using the molar volume 22.4 L/mol at STP, what is the molar mass of the gas?
questions.e: n = 2.24/22.4 = 0.1 mol, so M = 2.8/0.1 = 28 g/mol. 62.7 g/mol comes from multiplying 2.8 by 22.4 without dividing by the volume, and 56 g/mol doubles the correct value.

questions.s: How many moles of oxygen atoms are present in 0.3 mol of iron(III) sulfate, Fe₂(SO₄)₃?
questions.e: One formula unit contains 3 SO₄ groups, i.e. 3 × 4 = 12 O atoms, so n(O) = 0.3 × 12 = 3.6 mol. 1.2 mol counts only one sulfate group, and 0.9 mol counts sulfate groups instead of oxygen atoms.

questions.s: Which of the following is the approximate value of the Avogadro constant?
questions.e: The Avogadro constant is the number of particles per mole, NA ≈ 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹. 22.4 L/mol is the molar volume of a gas at STP, and 1.66 × 10⁻²⁴ g is the atomic mass unit, not a number per mole.

questions.s: 3.01 × 10²³ molecules of a gas have a mass of 8 g. What is the relative molecular mass of the gas? (NA = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹)
questions.e: n = 3.01 × 10²³ / 6.02 × 10²³ = 0.5 mol, so M = 8/0.5 = 16 g/mol and Mr = 16 (methane, for example). 4 comes from multiplying 8 by 0.5 instead of dividing.

questions.s: What mass of sulfur dioxide, SO₂, contains the same number of oxygen atoms as 36 g of water? (H = 1, O = 16, S = 32)
questions.e: n(H₂O) = 36/18 = 2 mol, which contains 2 mol O atoms. Each SO₂ has 2 O atoms, so 1 mol SO₂ = 64 g is needed. 128 g takes 2 mol of SO₂ and so doubles the oxygen.

questions.s: What is the total number of ions in 0.1 mol of sodium peroxide, Na₂O₂? (NA is the Avogadro constant)
questions.e: Na₂O₂ consists of 2 Na⁺ ions and one peroxide ion O₂²⁻ per formula unit, so 3 ions each: 0.1 × 3 = 0.3 mol = 0.3 NA. 0.4 NA wrongly treats the peroxide as two separate O²⁻ ions.

questions.s: Samples of SO₂ and SO₃ contain the same number of molecules. What is the ratio of the mass of SO₂ to the mass of SO₃? (O = 16, S = 32)
questions.e: Equal numbers of molecules means equal amounts, so the mass ratio equals the molar mass ratio 64 : 80 = 4 : 5. 2 : 3 is the ratio of oxygen atoms, and 5 : 4 is the inverse.

questions.s: What volume does 0.5 mol of oxygen gas occupy at STP? (Use the molar volume 22.4 L/mol at STP.)
questions.e: V = n × Vm = 0.5 × 22.4 = 11.2 L. 22.4 L is the volume of a whole mole, and 5.6 L would be 0.25 mol.

questions.s: What amount of nitrogen gas is contained in 6.72 L of N₂ at STP? (Use the molar volume 22.4 L/mol at STP.)
questions.e: n = V/Vm = 6.72/22.4 = 0.3 mol. 0.6 mol counts nitrogen atoms instead of N₂ molecules, 3.33 mol inverts the ratio, and 150.5 mol multiplies instead of dividing.

questions.s: What volume does 8 g of methane, CH₄, occupy at STP? (H = 1, C = 12; use the molar volume 22.4 L/mol at STP.)
questions.e: M(CH₄) = 16 g/mol, so n = 8/16 = 0.5 mol and V = 0.5 × 22.4 = 11.2 L. 179.2 L comes from multiplying the mass directly by 22.4 without first converting grams to moles.

questions.s: What is the mass of 5.6 L of carbon dioxide at STP? (C = 12, O = 16; use the molar volume 22.4 L/mol at STP.)
questions.e: n = 5.6/22.4 = 0.25 mol, so m = 0.25 × 44 = 11 g. 22 g corresponds to 0.5 mol (11.2 L), and 44 g to a whole mole.

questions.s: Which statement about the molar volume of gases is correct?
o: One mole of water at STP occupies 22.4 L
The molar volume of a gas does not depend on temperature
The molar volume of a gas at STP depends on its molar mass
The molar volume of any gas at STP is about 22.4 L/mol
questions.e: At STP (0 °C, 101 kPa) one mole of any gas, pure or mixed, occupies about 22.4 L, whatever its molar mass. Water is not a gas at STP, so 22.4 L/mol does not apply to it, and molar volume increases with temperature.

questions.s: The density of a gas at STP is 1.25 g/L. What is its molar mass? (Use the molar volume 22.4 L/mol at STP.)
questions.e: M = ρ × Vm = 1.25 g/L × 22.4 L/mol = 28 g/mol. 17.9 g/mol comes from 22.4/1.25 and 0.056 g/mol from 1.25/22.4; both divide where they should multiply.

questions.s: Under the same temperature and pressure, the density of gas X is 22 times that of hydrogen gas, H₂. Which could X be? (H = 1, C = 12, N = 14, O = 16, S = 32)
questions.e: At the same T and p, density is proportional to molar mass, so M(X) = 22 × 2 = 44 g/mol, which is CO₂. Using 22 × 1 = 22 (taking H instead of H₂) fits none of them; NO₂ is 46 and SO₂ is 64.

questions.s: At the same temperature and pressure, 1 L of oxygen, O₂, and 1 L of methane, CH₄, are compared. Which quantity is the same for both?
questions.e: By Avogadro's law, equal volumes of gases at the same T and p contain equal numbers of molecules. The masses and densities differ because the molar masses (32 and 16) differ, and CH₄ has 5 atoms per molecule while O₂ has 2.

questions.s: At the same temperature and pressure, what is the ratio of the volume of 16 g of O₂ to the volume of 16 g of SO₂? (O = 16, S = 32)
questions.e: n(O₂) = 16/32 = 0.5 mol and n(SO₂) = 16/64 = 0.25 mol. Volume is proportional to amount, so V(O₂) : V(SO₂) = 0.5 : 0.25 = 2 : 1. 1 : 2 is the ratio of the molar masses, which is the inverse of the volume ratio for equal masses.

questions.s: A gas mixture contains 1.4 g of N₂ and 1.6 g of O₂. What is its total volume at STP? (N = 14, O = 16; use the molar volume 22.4 L/mol at STP.)
questions.e: n(N₂) = 1.4/28 = 0.05 mol and n(O₂) = 1.6/32 = 0.05 mol, so n(total) = 0.1 mol and V = 0.1 × 22.4 = 2.24 L. 1.12 L is the volume of only one of the two gases; 4.48 L uses atomic masses (14 and 16) as molar masses.

questions.s: A mixture of CO and CO₂ has an average molar mass of 32 g/mol. What is the volume ratio V(CO) : V(CO₂)? (C = 12, O = 16)
questions.e: Let x be the mole (volume) fraction of CO: 28x + 44(1 − x) = 32, so 16x = 12 and x = 0.75. Then CO : CO₂ = 0.75 : 0.25 = 3 : 1. 1 : 3 swaps the gases; since 32 is much closer to 28, CO must be the majority.

questions.s: At STP, 4.48 L of a mixture of N₂ and O₂ has a mass of 6.0 g. What is the mass of O₂ in the mixture? (N = 14, O = 16; use the molar volume 22.4 L/mol at STP.)
questions.e: n(total) = 4.48/22.4 = 0.2 mol. With a mol N₂ and b mol O₂: a + b = 0.2 and 28a + 32b = 6.0. Then 28(0.2) + 4b = 6.0 gives b = 0.1 mol, so m(O₂) = 3.2 g. 2.8 g is the mass of the N₂, not the O₂.

questions.s: Which equation correctly relates the pressure p, volume V, amount n and thermodynamic temperature T of an ideal gas (R is the gas constant)?
questions.e: The ideal gas equation is pV = nRT, with T in kelvin. It shows that at fixed n and T, p and V are inversely proportional; the other forms would make pressure grow with volume or fall with amount, which is wrong.

questions.s: A fixed amount of gas occupies 6 L at 100 kPa. At constant temperature the pressure is raised to 300 kPa. What is the new volume?
questions.e: At constant n and T, p₁V₁ = p₂V₂, so V₂ = 100 × 6/300 = 2 L. 18 L multiplies by the pressure ratio instead of dividing: higher pressure must give a smaller volume.

questions.s: A gas occupies 4.0 L at 27 °C. It is heated at constant pressure to 177 °C. What is its new volume?
questions.e: Temperatures must be in kelvin: 300 K and 450 K. At constant p, V/T is constant, so V₂ = 4.0 × 450/300 = 6.0 L. 26.2 L uses the Celsius ratio 177/27, and 2.7 L inverts the temperature ratio.

questions.s: A gas sample occupies 10 L at 249 kPa and 300 K. What amount of gas is present? (R = 8.3 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)
questions.e: Use SI units: p = 2.49 × 10⁵ Pa, V = 0.010 m³. n = pV/(RT) = (2.49 × 10⁵ × 0.010)/(8.3 × 300) = 2490/2490 = 1 mol. 1000 mol keeps V in litres with p in pascals, and 0.001 mol keeps p in kilopascals with V in m³.

questions.s: 0.5 mol of a gas is held in a 5.0 L container at 27 °C. What is its pressure? (R = 8.3 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)
questions.e: p = nRT/V = 0.5 × 8.3 × 300/(5.0 × 10⁻³) = 1245/0.005 = 2.49 × 10⁵ Pa = 249 kPa. 22.4 kPa uses 27 instead of 300 K, and 498 kPa forgets the factor 0.5 mol.

questions.s: 1.6 g of a gas occupies 2.0 L at 400 K and 83 kPa. What is its molar mass? (R = 8.3 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)
questions.e: n = pV/(RT) = (8.3 × 10⁴ Pa × 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³)/(8.3 × 400) = 166/3320 = 0.05 mol, so M = 1.6/0.05 = 32 g/mol. Both p and V must be in SI units (Pa and m³); mixing kPa with m³ or Pa with litres gives an answer wrong by a factor of 1000, not one of the listed values.

questions.s: Two identical sealed flasks at the same temperature contain 4 g of H₂ and 32 g of O₂ respectively. What is the ratio of the pressure in the H₂ flask to that in the O₂ flask? (H = 1, O = 16)
questions.e: At the same V and T, pressure is proportional to amount: n(H₂) = 4/2 = 2 mol and n(O₂) = 32/32 = 1 mol, so the ratio is 2 : 1. 1 : 8 is the ratio of the masses, which does not set the pressure.

questions.s: At the same temperature and pressure, which gas has the greatest density? (H = 1, C = 12, N = 14, O = 16, Cl = 35.5)
questions.e: At the same T and p, ρ = pM/(RT), so density is proportional to molar mass: Cl₂ 71, CO₂ 44, NH₃ 17, CH₄ 16. Cl₂ is the densest; CO₂ is often remembered as a heavy gas, but chlorine is heavier still.

questions.s: Under the same conditions, 10 mL of gas A₂ reacts exactly with 30 mL of gas B₂ to form 20 mL of a single gaseous product C. What is the formula of C?
questions.e: Volume ratios equal mole ratios, so A₂ + 3B₂ → 2C. Atom balance gives 2 A and 6 B in 2C, so C is AB₃. A₃B swaps the roles of A and B.

questions.s: What volume at STP is occupied by 1.204 × 10²³ molecules of chlorine gas, Cl₂? (NA = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹; use the molar volume 22.4 L/mol at STP.)
questions.e: n = 1.204 × 10²³ / 6.02 × 10²³ = 0.2 mol, so V = 0.2 × 22.4 = 4.48 L. 8.96 L treats the count as chlorine atoms that each occupy a molar volume, doubling the answer.

questions.s: Which of the following has the largest volume at STP? (H = 1, C = 12, N = 14, O = 16; NA = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹)
questions.e: 2 g H₂ is 1 mol of gas, 22.4 L at STP; 14 g N₂ and 3.01 × 10²³ CO₂ molecules are each 0.5 mol (11.2 L). 18 g of water is also 1 mol, but water is a liquid at STP, so it occupies only about 18 mL.

questions.s: A container filled with O₂ has a total mass of 116 g; filled with CO₂ at the same temperature and pressure it has a total mass of 122 g. Filled with gas X under the same conditions it has a total mass of 114 g. What is the relative molecular mass of X? (C = 12, O = 16)
questions.e: Equal volumes hold equal amounts n, so 44n − 32n = 122 − 116 gives n = 0.5 mol. The empty container is 116 − 0.5 × 32 = 100 g, so X has mass 14 g and M = 14/0.5 = 28. 14 takes the gas mass as the molar mass without dividing by 0.5 mol.

questions.s: A fixed amount of gas occupies 3 L at 100 kPa and 300 K. What is its volume at 150 kPa and 450 K?
questions.e: p₁V₁/T₁ = p₂V₂/T₂, so V₂ = 3 × (100/150) × (450/300) = 3 × (2/3) × (3/2) = 3 L. 2 L applies only the pressure change, 4.5 L only the temperature change, and 6.75 L uses the pressure ratio upside down.

questions.s: 0.2 mol of sodium chloride is dissolved in water to make 500 mL of solution. What is the concentration of the solution?
questions.e: c = n/V = 0.2 mol / 0.500 L = 0.4 mol/L. 0.1 mol/L multiplies by the volume instead of dividing, and 100 mol/L forgets to convert 500 mL to 0.500 L.

questions.s: What mass of sodium hydroxide is needed to prepare 250 mL of 0.4 mol/L NaOH solution? (H = 1, O = 16, Na = 23)
questions.e: n = cV = 0.4 × 0.250 = 0.1 mol, so m = 0.1 × 40 = 4.0 g. 16 g is the mass for a full litre of solution, and 10 g uses 0.25 mol (the volume number) as the amount.

questions.s: What is the concentration of chloride ions in 0.1 mol/L calcium chloride, CaCl₂, solution?
questions.e: CaCl₂ → Ca²⁺ + 2Cl⁻, so c(Cl⁻) = 2 × 0.1 = 0.2 mol/L. 0.3 mol/L is the total concentration of all ions, and 0.1 mol/L forgets the subscript 2.

questions.s: Which solution has the same chloride-ion concentration as 50 mL of 1 mol/L AlCl₃ solution?
questions.e: In 1 mol/L AlCl₃, c(Cl⁻) = 3 mol/L. KCl at 3 mol/L also gives 3 mol/L; CaCl₂ gives 4 mol/L, MgCl₂ gives 6 mol/L and NaCl gives 1 mol/L. 150 mL of 1 mol/L NaCl contains the same amount of Cl⁻ (0.15 mol), but concentration does not depend on volume.

questions.s: 10 g of sodium chloride is dissolved in 40 g of water. What is the mass fraction of NaCl in the solution?
questions.e: w = m(solute)/m(solution) = 10/(10 + 40) = 0.20 = 20 %. 25 % divides by the mass of water only instead of the mass of the whole solution.

questions.s: Fatima needs 200 g of a 15 % (by mass) glucose solution. What mass of water must she use?
questions.e: m(glucose) = 200 × 0.15 = 30 g, so m(water) = 200 − 30 = 170 g. 30 g is the mass of solute, and 185 g subtracts 15 g, treating the percentage as a mass.

questions.s: 50 mL of 2 mol/L hydrochloric acid is diluted with water to a final volume of 250 mL. What is the new concentration?
questions.e: c₁V₁ = c₂V₂, so c₂ = 2 × 50/250 = 0.4 mol/L. 0.5 mol/L would follow if 200 mL were the final volume (that is the water added), and 10 mol/L inverts the volume ratio: dilution must lower the concentration.

questions.s: What volume of 18 mol/L sulfuric acid is needed to prepare 500 mL of 0.9 mol/L H₂SO₄?
questions.e: n(H₂SO₄) = 0.9 × 0.500 = 0.45 mol, so V = 0.45/18 = 0.025 L = 25 mL. 2.5 mL and 250 mL are factor-of-ten slips in the unit conversion; using the whole 500 mL of concentrated acid would give 9 mol of H₂SO₄.

questions.s: What mass of water must be added to 50 g of 98 % sulfuric acid to obtain 20 % sulfuric acid?
questions.e: The mass of H₂SO₄ stays 50 × 0.98 = 49 g, so the final solution has mass 49/0.20 = 245 g. Water added = 245 − 50 = 195 g. 245 g is the mass of the final solution, not the water added.

questions.s: Concentrated hydrochloric acid has a mass fraction of HCl of 36.5 % and a density of 1.2 g/mL. What is its concentration? (H = 1, Cl = 35.5)
questions.e: Take 1 L = 1000 mL: mass = 1200 g, m(HCl) = 1200 × 0.365 = 438 g, n = 438/36.5 = 12 mol, so c = 12 mol/L (c = 1000ρw/M). 10 mol/L ignores the density and treats 1 L of solution as 1000 g.

questions.s: How many moles of Na⁺ are present in 200 mL of 0.5 mol/L sodium sulfate, Na₂SO₄, solution?
questions.e: n(Na₂SO₄) = 0.5 × 0.200 = 0.1 mol, and each formula unit gives 2 Na⁺, so n(Na⁺) = 0.2 mol. 0.1 mol is the amount of Na₂SO₄ (or of SO₄²⁻), and 0.3 mol counts all ions.

questions.s: 100 mL of 1 mol/L NaCl solution is mixed with 300 mL of 0.2 mol/L NaCl solution. Assuming the volumes add, what is the concentration of the mixture?
questions.e: n = 1 × 0.1 + 0.2 × 0.3 = 0.16 mol in 0.4 L, so c = 0.16/0.4 = 0.4 mol/L. 0.6 mol/L is the simple average of the two concentrations, which ignores that the volumes differ; 0.16 is the amount, not the concentration.

questions.s: In a solution of aluminium sulfate, Al₂(SO₄)₃, the concentration of Al³⁺ is 0.4 mol/L. What is the concentration of SO₄²⁻?
questions.e: The formula gives Al³⁺ : SO₄²⁻ = 2 : 3, so c(SO₄²⁻) = 0.4 × 3/2 = 0.6 mol/L. Charge balance agrees: 3 × 0.4 = 2 × 0.6. 0.27 mol/L uses the ratio upside down (× 2/3).

questions.s: Which piece of apparatus must be used to make up exactly 250 mL of a 0.1 mol/L standard solution?
questions.e: A volumetric flask is calibrated to contain one exact volume at its graduation mark, so it is used to make standard solutions. Beakers and conical flasks have only rough markings, and a measuring cylinder is not accurate enough for a standard solution.

questions.s: Kwame prepares a NaCl solution in a volumetric flask. Which mistake makes the concentration of his solution too high?
o: Some solution splashes out during the transfer
The flask is still wet with distilled water
Water is added past the graduation mark
He looks down on the mark from above when filling
questions.e: Looking down from above makes the meniscus seem to reach the mark too early, so the true volume is less than the flask volume and c = n/V is too high. Splashing loses solute (too low), adding too much water makes V too large (too low), and a wet flask has no effect because water is added to the mark anyway.

questions.s: What mass of copper(II) sulfate pentahydrate, CuSO₄·5H₂O, is needed to prepare 500 mL of 0.1 mol/L CuSO₄ solution? (H = 1, O = 16, S = 32, Cu = 64)
questions.e: n(CuSO₄) = 0.1 × 0.5 = 0.05 mol, and each mole of crystals gives one mole of CuSO₄, so m = 0.05 × 250 = 12.5 g. 8.0 g uses the molar mass of anhydrous CuSO₄ (160), ignoring the water of crystallisation.

questions.s: 22.4 L of hydrogen chloride gas, measured at STP, is dissolved in water to make 500 mL of hydrochloric acid. What is the concentration of the acid? (Use the molar volume 22.4 L/mol at STP.)
questions.e: n(HCl) = 22.4/22.4 = 1 mol, so c = 1/0.500 = 2 mol/L. 1 mol/L ignores the solution volume, and 0.5 mol/L divides the volume by the amount.

questions.s: 10 mL is taken from 1 L of 0.5 mol/L NaCl solution. Which statement about the 10 mL portion is correct?
questions.e: Taking a portion of a uniform solution does not change its concentration, which stays 0.5 mol/L. The amount in the portion is 0.5 × 0.010 = 0.005 mol. Reducing the concentration as well as the amount is the common mistake.

questions.s: A sodium hydroxide solution has a concentration of 6 mol/L and a density of 1.2 g/mL. What is the mass fraction of NaOH? (H = 1, O = 16, Na = 23)
questions.e: 1 L contains 6 × 40 = 240 g NaOH and has mass 1000 × 1.2 = 1200 g, so w = 240/1200 = 20 %. 24 % divides by 1000 g, i.e. ignores the density of the solution.

questions.s: 100 mL of 0.1 mol/L NaCl is mixed with 100 mL of 0.1 mol/L CaCl₂. Assuming the volumes add, what is the chloride-ion concentration of the mixture?
questions.e: n(Cl⁻) = 0.1 × 0.1 + 2 × 0.1 × 0.1 = 0.01 + 0.02 = 0.03 mol in 0.2 L, so c = 0.15 mol/L. 0.30 mol/L adds the concentrations (0.1 + 0.2) and forgets that the volume doubles.

questions.s: At a certain temperature a saturated potassium nitrate solution contains 25 g of KNO₃ for every 100 g of water. What is the mass fraction of KNO₃ in this saturated solution?
questions.e: w = 25/(25 + 100) = 25/125 = 20 %. 25 % divides by the mass of water only; the mass fraction must use the total mass of solution.

questions.s: 5.85 g of sodium chloride is dissolved in water and made up to 100 mL. What is the concentration of the solution? (Na = 23, Cl = 35.5)
questions.e: n = 5.85/58.5 = 0.1 mol, so c = 0.1/0.100 = 1 mol/L. 0.1 mol/L is the amount in moles, not the concentration, and 0.0585 mol/L divides the mass by 100 without using the molar mass.

questions.s: 20 mL of 5 mol/L NaOH is diluted to 100 mL, and then 10 mL of the diluted solution is taken. What amount of NaOH does the 10 mL contain?
questions.e: After dilution c = 5 × 20/100 = 1 mol/L, so 10 mL contains 1 × 0.010 = 0.01 mol. 0.05 mol forgets the dilution and uses 5 mol/L for the 10 mL; 0.1 mol is the whole amount of NaOH.

questions.s: 100 g of a 10 % salt solution is mixed with 300 g of a 30 % salt solution of the same salt. What is the mass fraction of salt in the mixture?
questions.e: m(salt) = 10 + 90 = 100 g in 400 g of solution, so w = 100/400 = 25 %. 20 % is the plain average of 10 % and 30 %, which ignores that there is three times more of the stronger solution.

questions.s: 500 mL of iron(III) sulfate solution contains 5.6 g of Fe³⁺. 100 mL of it is taken and diluted to 400 mL. What is the SO₄²⁻ concentration in the diluted solution? (Fe = 56)
questions.e: n(Fe³⁺) in 500 mL = 0.1 mol, so 100 mL contains 0.02 mol Fe³⁺ and 0.03 mol SO₄²⁻ (Fe : SO₄ = 2 : 3). Diluted to 0.4 L: c = 0.03/0.4 = 0.075 mol/L. 0.3 mol/L is the SO₄²⁻ concentration before dilution, and 0.05 mol/L is the Fe³⁺ concentration after dilution.

questions.s: For the reaction 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, what mass of oxygen is needed to burn 4 g of hydrogen completely? (H = 1, O = 16)
questions.e: n(H₂) = 4/2 = 2 mol, and the equation gives n(O₂) = 2/2 = 1 mol = 32 g. 64 g ignores the 2 : 1 mole ratio, and 36 g is the mass of water formed.

questions.s: 10 g of calcium carbonate reacts completely with excess hydrochloric acid: CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂. What volume of CO₂ is formed at STP? (C = 12, O = 16, Ca = 40; use the molar volume 22.4 L/mol at STP.)
questions.e: n(CaCO₃) = 10/100 = 0.1 mol, which gives 0.1 mol CO₂, i.e. 0.1 × 22.4 = 2.24 L. 4.48 L wrongly uses the coefficient 2 of HCl for the CO₂.

questions.s: 6.5 g of zinc reacts completely with excess dilute sulfuric acid: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂. What mass of hydrogen is produced? (H = 1, Zn = 65)
questions.e: n(Zn) = 6.5/65 = 0.1 mol, which gives 0.1 mol H₂ with mass 0.1 × 2 = 0.2 g. 0.1 g uses 1 g/mol for H₂ instead of 2 g/mol.

questions.s: Under the same conditions, nitrogen reacts completely with hydrogen: N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃. What volume of hydrogen reacts with 10 L of nitrogen?
questions.e: For gases at the same T and p, volume ratios equal mole ratios, so V(H₂) = 3 × 10 = 30 L. 20 L is the volume of ammonia formed, not the hydrogen used.

questions.s: 24.5 g of potassium chlorate decomposes completely: 2KClO₃ → 2KCl + 3O₂. What mass of oxygen gas is released? (O = 16, Cl = 35.5, K = 39)
questions.e: M(KClO₃) = 122.5 g/mol, so n = 0.2 mol and n(O₂) = 0.2 × 3/2 = 0.3 mol = 9.6 g. 6.4 g assumes a 1 : 1 ratio, and 4.8 g uses 16 g/mol (O atoms) instead of 32 g/mol for O₂.

questions.s: 3 mol of H₂ and 2 mol of O₂ are ignited: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. What amount of water is formed?
questions.e: 3 mol H₂ needs only 1.5 mol O₂, so H₂ is the limiting reagent and gives 3 mol H₂O (0.5 mol O₂ is left over). 4 mol assumes all the O₂ reacts, which would need 4 mol H₂.

questions.s: 5.6 g of iron is heated with 4.8 g of sulfur: Fe + S → FeS. What mass of iron(II) sulfide forms? (S = 32, Fe = 56)
questions.e: n(Fe) = 0.1 mol and n(S) = 0.15 mol, so Fe is limiting and 0.1 mol FeS = 8.8 g forms, with 1.6 g of sulfur left over. 10.4 g adds both masses, which is valid only if neither reactant is in excess; 13.2 g bases the answer on the sulfur.

questions.s: 28 g of nitrogen reacts with excess hydrogen, N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃, and 17 g of ammonia is obtained. What is the percentage yield? (H = 1, N = 14)
questions.e: n(N₂) = 1 mol gives a theoretical 2 mol NH₃ = 34 g, so yield = 17/34 × 100 % = 50 %. 60.7 % divides the product mass by the reactant mass (17/28), which is not a yield, and 100 % forgets the factor 2 in the equation.

questions.s: 50 g of calcium carbonate is heated, CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂, and the yield of calcium oxide is 80 %. What mass of CaO is obtained? (C = 12, O = 16, Ca = 40)
questions.e: n(CaCO₃) = 0.5 mol, so the theoretical mass of CaO is 0.5 × 56 = 28 g, and the actual mass is 0.8 × 28 = 22.4 g. 28.0 g is the theoretical yield, 17.6 g is 80 % of the CO₂ mass, and 40.0 g is 80 % of the reactant mass.

questions.s: Aluminium reacts with acid and with alkali: 2Al + 6HCl → 2AlCl₃ + 3H₂ and 2Al + 2NaOH + 2H₂O → 2NaAlO₂ + 3H₂. Two equal masses of aluminium react separately with excess hydrochloric acid and with excess NaOH solution. What is the ratio of the volumes of H₂ produced (same conditions)?
questions.e: In both equations 2 mol Al gives 3 mol H₂, so equal amounts of Al give equal amounts, and equal volumes, of H₂. 3 : 1 compares the amounts of HCl and NaOH consumed (6 : 2), not the hydrogen produced.

questions.s: 5.1 g of a magnesium-aluminium alloy reacts with excess hydrochloric acid and gives 5.6 L of H₂ at STP. What mass of aluminium is in the alloy? (Mg = 24, Al = 27; use the molar volume 22.4 L/mol at STP.)
questions.e: n(H₂) = 0.25 mol. With x mol Mg (1 H₂ each) and y mol Al (1.5 H₂ each): 24x + 27y = 5.1 and x + 1.5y = 0.25. Solving gives y = 0.1 and x = 0.1, so m(Al) = 2.7 g. 2.4 g is the mass of magnesium, and 2.55 g simply halves the alloy mass.

questions.s: Propane burns completely: C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O. What volume of oxygen is needed to burn 2 L of propane, both volumes measured under the same conditions?
questions.e: Volume ratio = mole ratio, so V(O₂) = 5 × 2 = 10 L. 5 L reads the coefficient as the answer without scaling to 2 L of propane, and 6 L is the volume of CO₂ formed.

questions.s: 10 mL of H₂ and 10 mL of O₂ are mixed and ignited, then cooled back to room temperature and pressure so that the water is liquid. What gas remains?
questions.e: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, so 10 mL H₂ uses only 5 mL O₂, leaving 5 mL of O₂. H₂ is the limiting reagent, so none of it remains, and the water condenses to a liquid at room temperature.

questions.s: In the reaction A + 2B → C + D, 8 g of A reacts exactly with 10 g of B to form 6 g of C. What mass of D is formed?
questions.e: By conservation of mass, m(D) = 8 + 10 − 6 = 12 g. The coefficient 2 refers to moles, not grams, so it does not change the mass balance; 24 g wrongly doubles the result.

questions.s: In the reaction 2A + B → 2C, 6 g of A reacts exactly with 2 g of B. The relative molecular mass of B is 32. What is the relative molecular mass of A?
questions.e: n(B) = 2/32 = 1/16 mol, so n(A) = 2 × 1/16 = 1/8 mol and M(A) = 6 ÷ (1/8) = 48 g/mol. 96 ignores the coefficient 2 and treats n(A) as 1/16 mol.

questions.s: What volume of 0.5 mol/L sulfuric acid exactly neutralises 20 mL of 1 mol/L NaOH? (2NaOH + H₂SO₄ → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O)
questions.e: n(NaOH) = 0.020 mol, so n(H₂SO₄) = 0.010 mol and V = 0.010/0.5 = 0.020 L = 20 mL. 40 mL assumes a 1 : 1 ratio, forgetting that each H₂SO₄ neutralises two NaOH.

questions.s: In a titration, 25.0 mL of hydrochloric acid is exactly neutralised by 20.0 mL of 0.25 mol/L NaOH. What is the concentration of the acid?
questions.e: n(NaOH) = 0.25 × 0.020 = 0.005 mol = n(HCl), so c(HCl) = 0.005/0.025 = 0.2 mol/L. 0.3125 mol/L uses the volumes the wrong way round; the acid needed more volume, so it must be the more dilute solution.

questions.s: 0.3 mol of copper reacts completely with dilute nitric acid: 3Cu + 8HNO₃ → 3Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2NO↑ + 4H₂O. What volume of NO is released at STP? (Use the molar volume 22.4 L/mol at STP.)
questions.e: n(NO) = 0.3 × 2/3 = 0.2 mol, so V = 0.2 × 22.4 = 4.48 L. Assuming one NO per Cu would give 6.72 L, and 2.24 L halves the correct amount.

questions.s: Sulfur burns in oxygen: S + O₂ → SO₂. What mass of sulfur dioxide is formed when 1.6 g of sulfur burns completely? (O = 16, S = 32)
questions.e: n(S) = 1.6/32 = 0.05 mol, which gives 0.05 mol SO₂ = 0.05 × 64 = 3.2 g. 1.6 g forgets the mass of oxygen that combines with the sulfur.

questions.s: 12.5 g of impure limestone reacts with excess hydrochloric acid and gives 2.24 L of CO₂ at STP. The impurities do not react. What is the percentage by mass of CaCO₃ in the limestone? (C = 12, O = 16, Ca = 40; use the molar volume 22.4 L/mol at STP.)
questions.e: n(CO₂) = 0.1 mol = n(CaCO₃), so m(CaCO₃) = 10 g and purity = 10/12.5 × 100 % = 80 %. 35.2 % divides the mass of CO₂ (4.4 g) by the sample mass, which is not the carbonate content.

questions.s: 10 g of sodium hydroxide is added to a solution containing 0.2 mol of HCl. After the reaction, which substance is left over? (H = 1, O = 16, Na = 23)
questions.e: n(NaOH) = 10/40 = 0.25 mol reacts 1 : 1 with 0.2 mol HCl, so HCl is limiting and 0.05 mol NaOH = 2 g is left. Only 0.2 mol NaCl forms, since the amount of product is set by the limiting reagent.

questions.s: 4.6 g of sodium reacts completely with water, 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂, and the solution is made up to 200 mL. What is the concentration of NaOH? (Na = 23)
questions.e: n(Na) = 0.2 mol gives 0.2 mol NaOH, so c = 0.2/0.200 = 1 mol/L. 0.5 mol/L follows from wrongly taking one NaOH per two Na (confusing it with the H₂ ratio).

questions.s: A product C is made in two steps, A → B with a yield of 80 % and then B → C with a yield of 50 % (1 mol of B gives at most 1 mol of C, and 1 mol of A gives at most 1 mol of B). What is the overall yield of C from A?
questions.e: Yields multiply: 0.80 × 0.50 = 0.40, i.e. 40 %. 65 % is the average of the two yields, which overstates the result, because the losses of each step add up.

questions.s: 5.4 g of aluminium is heated with 24 g of iron(III) oxide: 2Al + Fe₂O₃ → Al₂O₃ + 2Fe. What mass of iron is formed? (O = 16, Al = 27, Fe = 56)
questions.e: n(Al) = 0.2 mol needs 0.1 mol Fe₂O₃, but 0.15 mol is present, so Al is limiting. n(Fe) = n(Al) = 0.2 mol = 11.2 g. 16.8 g is based on all the Fe₂O₃ reacting (0.3 mol Fe), which is impossible with only 0.2 mol Al.

questions.s: 30 mL of a mixture of methane and hydrogen needs exactly 45 mL of oxygen for complete combustion (all volumes at the same conditions): CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O and 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. What volume of methane is in the mixture?
questions.e: Let x = V(CH₄) and y = V(H₂): x + y = 30 and 2x + 0.5y = 45. Substituting y = 30 − x gives 1.5x = 30, so x = 20 mL. 10 mL is the volume of hydrogen, not methane.

questions.s: What is the mass fraction of nitrogen in ammonium nitrate, NH₄NO₃? (H = 1, N = 14, O = 16)
questions.e: Mr(NH₄NO₃) = 80 and the formula contains 2 N atoms, so w(N) = 28/80 = 35 %. 17.5 % counts only one nitrogen atom, and 60 % is the mass fraction of oxygen.

questions.s: A sample contains 1.204 × 10²⁴ molecules. What amount of substance is this? (NA = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹)
questions.e: n = N/NA = 1.204 × 10²⁴ / 6.02 × 10²³ = 2 mol. 0.5 mol divides NA by N, the inverse ratio, and 20 mol is a power-of-ten slip.

questions.s: Which is the usual unit of molar mass?
questions.e: Molar mass is the mass per mole of substance, M = m/n, so its unit is g/mol. Relative molecular mass has no unit, g is a unit of mass, and mol/L is a unit of concentration.

questions.s: What is the mass of 1.5 mol of oxygen gas, O₂? (O = 16)
questions.e: M(O₂) = 32 g/mol, so m = 1.5 × 32 = 48 g. 24 g uses 16 g/mol, the molar mass of oxygen atoms rather than O₂ molecules, and 32 g is the mass of only 1 mol.

questions.s: What does a concentration of 1 mol/L mean for a solution?
o: 1 mol of solute in 1 L of solution
1 mol of solute dissolved in 1 L of water
1 g of solute in 1 L of solution
1 mol of solute in 1 kg of water
questions.e: Amount concentration is the amount of solute per litre of solution, c = n/V(solution). Dissolving 1 mol in 1 L of water gives a volume that is not exactly 1 L, so the concentration would not be exactly 1 mol/L.

questions.s: Equal amounts (in moles) of carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide are compared. What is the ratio of the number of oxygen atoms in CO to that in CO₂?
questions.e: Equal amounts mean equal numbers of molecules; CO has 1 O atom and CO₂ has 2, so the ratio is 1 : 2. 7 : 11 is the mass ratio (28 : 44), and 1 : 1 is the ratio of molecules or of carbon atoms.

questions.s: The molar volume 22.4 L/mol applies to gases at STP. Which conditions does STP refer to here?
questions.e: STP in this sense means 0 °C (273 K) and about 101 kPa (1 atm). At 25 °C and 101 kPa the molar volume is larger, about 24.5 L/mol, so 22.4 L/mol must not be used there.

questions.s: What mass of potassium chloride is present in 500 mL of 0.2 mol/L KCl solution? (Cl = 35.5, K = 39)
questions.e: n = 0.2 × 0.500 = 0.1 mol and M(KCl) = 74.5 g/mol, so m = 7.45 g. 14.9 g is the mass for 1 L of solution, and 37.25 g treats the volume 0.5 as the amount.

questions.s: Which sample has the greatest mass? (H = 1, C = 12, O = 16, Na = 23, Cl = 35.5; NA = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹)
questions.e: Masses: H₂O 0.5 × 18 = 9 g, CH₄ 1 × 16 = 16 g, NaCl 0.1 × 58.5 = 5.85 g, CO₂ 0.5 × 44 = 22 g. The methane sample has the largest amount, but the CO₂ sample is heaviest because of its large molar mass.

questions.s: An organic compound contains 40.0 % carbon, 6.7 % hydrogen and 53.3 % oxygen by mass, and its relative molecular mass is 60. What is its molecular formula? (H = 1, C = 12, O = 16)
questions.e: Mole ratio C : H : O = 40.0/12 : 6.7/1 : 53.3/16 = 3.33 : 6.7 : 3.33 = 1 : 2 : 1, so the empirical formula is CH₂O (Mr 30). Since 60/30 = 2, the molecular formula is C₂H₄O₂. C₃H₈O also has Mr 60 but is 60 % carbon, so it does not fit the data.

questions.s: What is the density of oxygen gas, O₂, at 249 kPa and 300 K? (O = 16; R = 8.3 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)
questions.e: From pV = nRT, ρ = pM/(RT) = (2.49 × 10⁵ × 0.032)/(8.3 × 300) = 7968/2490 = 3.2 kg/m³ = 3.2 g/L. 1.43 g/L is the density at STP (32/22.4), which does not apply at these conditions.

questions.s: NA is the Avogadro constant. Which statement is correct? (O = 16)
o: 16 g of a mixture of O₂ and O₃ contains NA oxygen atoms
At STP, 22.4 L of water contains NA molecules
1 mol/L NaCl solution contains NA sodium ions
At room temperature and pressure, 11.2 L of N₂ contains 0.5 NA molecules
questions.e: Both O₂ and O₃ consist only of O atoms, so 16 g of any mixture contains 16/16 = 1 mol of O atoms, i.e. NA. Water is not a gas at STP, the NaCl statement gives no volume, and 22.4 L/mol applies only at STP, not at room temperature.

questions.s: NA is the Avogadro constant. Which statement is correct? (D = ²H = 2, O = 16, Na = 23)
o: 1 mol of Cl₂ reacting completely with iron gains NA electrons
18 g of heavy water, D₂O, contains 10 NA electrons
0.1 mol of Fe reacting with excess hydrochloric acid loses 0.3 NA electrons
2.3 g of Na reacting completely with oxygen loses 0.1 NA electrons
questions.e: 0.1 mol Na always becomes Na⁺, whatever the product (Na₂O or Na₂O₂), so it loses 0.1 NA electrons. Cl₂ → 2Cl⁻ gains 2 NA electrons per mole; M(D₂O) = 20, so 18 g is 0.9 mol with 9 NA electrons; Fe with HCl gives Fe²⁺, so 0.2 NA electrons.

questions.s: An open flask of air is heated from 27 °C to 127 °C while the pressure stays constant. What fraction of the air originally in the flask escapes?
questions.e: At constant p and V, n is proportional to 1/T, so n₂/n₁ = 300 K/400 K = 3/4 and 1/4 escapes. 1/3 compares the escaped gas with the gas remaining instead of the original amount, and 100/127 wrongly uses Celsius temperatures.

questions.s: 100 mL of 0.2 mol/L BaCl₂ is mixed with 100 mL of 0.3 mol/L Na₂SO₄. What mass of BaSO₄ precipitates? (Mr of BaSO₄ = 233)
questions.e: n(Ba²⁺) = 0.02 mol and n(SO₄²⁻) = 0.03 mol react 1 : 1, so Ba²⁺ is limiting and 0.02 × 233 = 4.66 g precipitates. 6.99 g is based on the sulfate, which is in excess, and 11.65 g adds both amounts.

questions.s: 2.86 g of hydrated sodium carbonate, Na₂CO₃·xH₂O, is heated until all the water is lost, leaving 1.06 g of Na₂CO₃. What is x? (H = 1, C = 12, O = 16, Na = 23)
questions.e: n(Na₂CO₃) = 1.06/106 = 0.01 mol and m(water) = 2.86 − 1.06 = 1.80 g = 0.1 mol, so x = 0.1/0.01 = 10. Dividing masses (1.80/1.06 ≈ 1.7) instead of amounts gives a meaningless value near 1 or 2.

questions.s: 10.0 g of a mixture of Na₂CO₃ and NaHCO₃ is heated to constant mass, 2NaHCO₃ → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂, leaving 6.9 g of solid. What is the mass fraction of NaHCO₃ in the original mixture? (H = 1, C = 12, O = 16, Na = 23)
questions.e: 2 mol NaHCO₃ (168 g) loses H₂O + CO₂ = 62 g. The loss is 3.1 g, so m(NaHCO₃) = 3.1 × 168/62 = 8.4 g, which is 84 %. 31 % is the percentage mass loss, and 16 % is the share of Na₂CO₃.

questions.s: 20 mL of CO and 20 mL of O₂ are mixed and ignited: 2CO + O₂ → 2CO₂. All volumes are measured at the same temperature and pressure. By how much does the total gas volume decrease?
questions.e: 20 mL CO uses 10 mL O₂ and forms 20 mL CO₂, so the final gas is 20 mL CO₂ + 10 mL O₂ = 30 mL. The decrease is 40 − 30 = 10 mL. 30 mL is the final volume, not the decrease.

questions.s: Equal volumes of 10 % and 50 % sulfuric acid (mass fractions) are mixed. The denser solution is the more concentrated one. What is the mass fraction of H₂SO₄ in the mixture?
questions.e: Equal volumes do not have equal masses: the 50 % acid is denser, so it contributes more mass to the mixture. The mass-weighted average therefore lies above the simple average of 30 %. Exactly 30 % would need equal masses, not equal volumes.

questions.s: A rigid container holds 0.2 mol of helium at pressure p. Oxygen is added at the same temperature until the pressure is 3p. What mass of oxygen was added? (O = 16)
questions.e: At fixed V and T, p ∝ n(total), so the final amount is 3 × 0.2 = 0.6 mol and the added O₂ is 0.4 mol = 12.8 g. 19.2 g counts the whole 0.6 mol as oxygen, forgetting the helium already present.

questions.s: What is the relative formula mass of calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)₂? (H = 1, O = 16, Ca = 40)
questions.e: Mr = 40 + 2 × (16 + 1) = 40 + 34 = 74. 57 ignores the subscript 2 outside the bracket, and 58 applies it to hydrogen only.

questions.s: What amount of sodium chloride is present in 11.7 g of NaCl? (Na = 23, Cl = 35.5)
questions.e: M(NaCl) = 58.5 g/mol, so n = 11.7/58.5 = 0.2 mol. 5 mol is the inverted ratio 58.5/11.7.

questions.s: How many molecules are present in 2 mol of carbon dioxide? (NA = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹)
questions.e: N = n × NA = 2 × 6.02 × 10²³ = 1.204 × 10²⁴ molecules. 3.612 × 10²⁴ is the number of atoms, since each CO₂ molecule has 3 atoms.

questions.s: What volume does 0.25 mol of nitrogen gas occupy at STP? (Use the molar volume 22.4 L/mol at STP.)
