questions.e: Iron rusts only when water and oxygen are both present: iron in dry air or in boiled water without dissolved oxygen does not rust. Salt speeds up rusting but is not essential, and nitrogen takes no part.

questions.s: Hydrogen is passed over heated black copper(II) oxide. What is observed?
o: The black solid turns red and water droplets form
The black solid turns white and a brown gas forms
The black solid turns blue and melts
The black solid turns yellow and a gas burns
questions.e: CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O: hydrogen reduces the black oxide to red-brown copper metal, and water vapour condenses as droplets in the cooler part of the tube. Blue would mean hydrated copper(II) salts, which cannot form here.

questions.s: A solution of copper(II) chloride is held in a flame on a clean platinum wire. What colour is the flame?
questions.e: Copper compounds give a green or blue-green flame, which is why they are used for green fireworks. Yellow is the colour for sodium, lilac for potassium and brick-red for calcium.

questions.s: 10.0 g of a mixture of copper and copper(II) oxide is heated in air until all the copper is oxidised. The mass rises to 11.6 g. What mass of copper was in the mixture? (Cu = 64, O = 16)
questions.e: 2Cu + O₂ → 2CuO: the mass gain is the oxygen taken up, 1.6 g = 0.1 mol O atoms, so 0.1 mol Cu = 6.4 g was present. 8.0 g is the mass of CuO formed from that copper, not the copper itself.

questions.s: Which ionic equation correctly shows chlorine reacting with water?
questions.e: Cl₂ + H₂O ⇌ HCl + HClO; HCl is a strong acid and is written as ions, but HClO is a weak acid and stays as molecules. Writing ClO⁻ treats HClO as fully ionised, which is the common error. Free O atoms and H₂O₂ are not formed.

questions.s: Which of the following is NOT a use of chlorine?
questions.e: Chlorine kills microbes in water, is turned into NaClO bleach, and is a raw material for PVC (polyvinyl chloride). Weather balloons need a gas much less dense than air, such as helium or hydrogen; chlorine is denser than air and poisonous.

questions.s: Chlorine reacts with hot concentrated NaOH solution: 3Cl₂ + 6NaOH → 5NaCl + NaClO₃ + 3H₂O. What is the ratio of chlorine atoms reduced to chlorine atoms oxidised?
questions.e: Of the 6 Cl atoms, 5 go from 0 to −1 (in NaCl), so they are reduced, gaining 5 electrons; 1 goes from 0 to +5 (in NaClO₃), losing 5 electrons. Ratio reduced : oxidised = 5 : 1. Answering 1 : 1 applies the cold-alkali reaction, where NaCl and NaClO form in equal amounts.

questions.s: How is bleaching powder made industrially?
o: Passing chlorine into slaked lime, Ca(OH)₂
Passing chlorine into a suspension of chalk, CaCO₃
questions.e: 2Cl₂ + 2Ca(OH)₂ → CaCl₂ + Ca(ClO)₂ + 2H₂O, using solid slaked lime or lime milk. Limewater is a very dilute solution (Ca(OH)₂ is only slightly soluble), so it would give very little product. Heating CaCl₂ in oxygen does not produce hypochlorite.

questions.s: Which liquid is best for washing solid sulfur out of a test tube?
questions.e: Sulfur is a yellow molecular solid that is insoluble in water, only slightly soluble in ethanol, and readily soluble in carbon disulfide, CS₂. Dilute acids do not react with sulfur. (Hot NaOH solution can also be used, as it reacts with sulfur.)

questions.s: SO₂ is bubbled into BaCl₂ solution and no precipitate forms. Which substance, added afterwards, would produce a white precipitate?
questions.e: H₂SO₃ is weaker than HCl, so BaSO₃ cannot form in the acidic solution. H₂O₂ oxidises the sulfur(IV) to sulfate: SO₂ + H₂O₂ → H₂SO₄, and then Ba²⁺ + SO₄²⁻ → BaSO₄, which is insoluble even in acid. Adding HCl makes the solution more acidic and still gives no precipitate.

questions.s: Which sulfur species can act as both an oxidising agent and a reducing agent?
questions.e: Sulfur in SO₂ is +4, between its lowest (−2) and highest (+6) states, so it can be reduced (2H₂S + SO₂ → 3S + 2H₂O) or oxidised (to SO₃ or SO₄²⁻). In H₂S sulfur is −2 and can only be oxidised, while in H₂SO₄ and Na₂SO₄ it is +6 and can only be reduced.

questions.s: Carbon is heated with concentrated sulfuric acid, and the gases are tested for CO₂ with limewater. Why must all the SO₂ be removed before the gas reaches the limewater?
o: SO₂ reacts with CO₂ and destroys it
SO₂ is denser than CO₂ and would block the tube
questions.e: C + 2H₂SO₄ → CO₂ + 2SO₂ + 2H₂O. SO₂ + Ca(OH)₂ → CaSO₃ + H₂O also gives a white precipitate, so a milky result would not prove CO₂. SO₂ is removed with acidified KMnO₄, and magenta solution confirms it has gone before the limewater test.

questions.s: Which reaction is an example of nitrogen fixation?
questions.e: Nitrogen fixation means converting free nitrogen, N₂, into nitrogen compounds, as in the Haber process (or lightning and root bacteria). The other reactions only convert one nitrogen compound into another, so no free N₂ is fixed.

questions.s: How should nitrogen monoxide, NO, be collected in the laboratory?
o: In an upright jar by displacing air
In an inverted jar by displacing air
questions.e: NO is almost insoluble in water but reacts at once with oxygen in air (2NO + O₂ → 2NO₂), and its density is close to that of air, so it must be collected over water. NO₂, by contrast, reacts with water and is collected by displacing air.

questions.s: Which nitrogen fertiliser has the highest mass percentage of nitrogen? (H = 1, C = 12, N = 14, O = 16, S = 32)
questions.e: Urea: 28/60 ≈ 46.7 %. NH₄NO₃: 28/80 = 35 %. (NH₄)₂SO₄: 28/132 ≈ 21.2 %. NH₄HCO₃: 14/79 ≈ 17.7 %. Ammonium nitrate is a tempting choice because it has two N atoms, but urea has the same two N atoms in a lighter molecule.

questions.s: A tube containing 40 mL of NO is inverted in water. Oxygen is then passed in slowly. What volume of O₂ must be added for water to fill the tube completely?
questions.e: Overall, 4NO + 3O₂ + 2H₂O → 4HNO₃ (from 2NO + O₂ → 2NO₂ and 3NO₂ + H₂O → 2HNO₃ + NO). So 40 mL NO needs 40 × 3/4 = 30 mL O₂. Answering 20 mL uses only the first step, 2NO + O₂ → 2NO₂, ignoring the NO regenerated in water.

questions.s: Activated charcoal is used in water filters and gas masks. How does it remove unwanted substances?
o: It oxidises them to carbon dioxide
It dissolves them into the charcoal
It reacts with them to form salts
Its huge porous surface adsorbs them
questions.e: Activated charcoal is full of tiny pores, giving a very large surface area per gram, so molecules of coloured or smelly substances stick to its surface (adsorption). This is a physical process; no chemical reaction or oxidation takes place.

questions.s: To show that carbonic acid is stronger than silicic acid, CO₂ made from marble and hydrochloric acid is passed into Na₂SiO₃ solution. Why should the gas first pass through saturated NaHCO₃ solution?
o: To remove any oxygen in the gas
To produce extra carbon dioxide for the test
To remove HCl, which could itself precipitate silicic acid
questions.e: Hydrochloric acid is volatile, and HCl gas would react with Na₂SiO₃ (2HCl + Na₂SiO₃ → H₂SiO₃ + 2NaCl), so the precipitate would not prove anything about carbonic acid. NaHCO₃ removes HCl (HCl + NaHCO₃ → NaCl + H₂O + CO₂) without absorbing CO₂. An aqueous solution cannot dry a gas.

questions.s: What does the term 'white pollution' refer to?
o: Dust from lime and cement works
Waste plastics that do not break down
questions.e: 'White pollution' refers to discarded plastic bags, foam boxes and films, which degrade extremely slowly and litter land and water. It is reduced by using less plastic, recycling and degradable plastics. Smoke and dust are forms of air pollution.

questions.s: Which general formula describes the open-chain alkanes?
questions.e: Alkanes are saturated: every carbon forms four single bonds, so each extra CH₂ adds to a chain capped by two extra H atoms, e.g. CH₄, C₂H₆, C₃H₈. CₙH₂ₙ fits alkenes and cycloalkanes, which have one double bond or one ring. CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ fits alkynes and CₙH₂ₙ₋₆ fits benzene and its homologues.

questions.s: How many structural isomers have the molecular formula C₅H₁₂?
questions.e: The isomers are pentane CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃, 2-methylbutane (CH₃)₂CHCH₂CH₃ and 2,2-dimethylpropane C(CH₃)₄. A chain drawn as '3-methylbutane' is the same molecule as 2-methylbutane numbered from the other end, so counting it again gives the wrong total of 4.

questions.s: A mixture of methane and chlorine is exposed to ultraviolet light, and CH₃Cl and HCl are formed. What type of reaction is this?
questions.e: One H atom of CH₄ is replaced by a Cl atom: CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl, which is substitution; light splits Cl₂ into Cl radicals that start a chain reaction. Addition needs a C=C or C≡C bond, which methane does not have.

questions.s: How many moles of O₂ are needed for the complete combustion of 1 mol of propane, C₃H₈?
questions.e: C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O. The products contain 3 × 2 + 4 × 1 = 10 O atoms, which is 5 mol O₂. Choosing 3 or 4 means counting only the CO₂ or only the H₂O, and 7 is the total moles of products, not of oxygen.

questions.s: Which compound quickly decolourises bromine water at room temperature?
questions.e: Propene has a C=C double bond, and Br₂ adds across it to give colourless CH₃CHBrCH₂Br. Ethane and chloroethane are saturated and react with bromine only in light by slow substitution; acetic acid has no C=C bond either.

questions.s: Propene, CH₃CH=CH₂, reacts with hydrogen bromide. What is the major product?
questions.e: By Markovnikov's rule the H atom adds to the CH₂ end (the carbon that already has more H atoms) and Br adds to the middle carbon, giving 2-bromopropane. 1-bromopropane is only the minor product here. CH₂BrCHBrCH₃ would come from adding Br₂, not HBr.

questions.s: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₃?
questions.e: The longest chain has 4 carbons (butane), with a methyl branch. Numbering from the end nearer the branch puts it on C2, so the name is 2-methylbutane. '3-methylbutane' numbers from the wrong end, and '2-ethylpropane' does not use the longest chain.

questions.s: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂C(CH₃)₂CH₃?
questions.e: The longest chain is CH₃–CH₂–C–CH₃, four carbons, with two methyl groups on one carbon. Numbering from the right gives that carbon position 2, so the name is 2,2-dimethylbutane. Numbering from the left gives the higher locants 3,3, which IUPAC rules reject.

questions.s: Which of the following is an addition reaction?
questions.e: In the hydration of ethene the two reactants join into a single product as H and OH add across the C=C bond, which is addition. The methane reaction is substitution, the ethanol reaction is elimination (dehydration), and the last one is esterification, a condensation that releases water.

questions.s: Which compound can exist as cis and trans isomers?
questions.e: Cis-trans isomerism needs two different groups on each carbon of the C=C bond. In but-2-ene each double-bond carbon carries H and CH₃, so the methyl groups can be on the same side (cis) or opposite sides (trans). In the other three compounds at least one double-bond carbon has two identical groups (two H, two Cl or two CH₃).

questions.s: What is the H–C–C bond angle in ethyne, HC≡CH?
questions.e: Each carbon in ethyne has two electron domains (the triple bond and the C–H bond), so the molecule is linear and the angle is 180°. 120° is the angle around the C=C carbons in ethene, and 109.5° is the tetrahedral angle in alkanes.

questions.s: Calcium carbide, CaC₂, is added to water in the laboratory. Which flammable gas is produced?
questions.e: CaC₂ + 2H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + C₂H₂. The C₂²⁻ ion takes two H⁺ from water to form ethyne (acetylene), HC≡CH. Ethene is made by dehydrating ethanol, not from carbide.

questions.s: Ethyne reacts completely with excess bromine to give a saturated product. How many moles of Br₂ react with 1 mol of ethyne?
questions.e: The triple bond contains two π bonds, each of which adds one Br₂: HC≡CH + 2Br₂ → CHBr₂CHBr₂ (1,1,2,2-tetrabromoethane). Answering 1 stops at CHBr=CHBr, which still has a C=C bond and is not saturated.

questions.s: 0.1 mol of a gaseous hydrocarbon burns completely to give 0.3 mol of CO₂ and 0.2 mol of H₂O. What is its molecular formula?
questions.e: Each molecule gives 0.3/0.1 = 3 CO₂, so 3 C atoms, and 0.2/0.1 = 2 H₂O, so 4 H atoms: C₃H₄ (for example propyne). C₃H₈ comes from forgetting that each H₂O contains two H atoms and using 0.2 × 4 by mistake; C₃H₆ would give 0.3 mol H₂O.

questions.s: 4.2 g of an alkene reacts exactly with 16.0 g of Br₂. What is the molecular formula of the alkene? (Br = 80, C = 12, H = 1)
questions.e: One C=C bond adds one Br₂, so n(alkene) = n(Br₂) = 16.0/160 = 0.10 mol. Mr = 4.2/0.10 = 42, and 14n = 42 gives n = 3, so C₃H₆. Using 80 as the molar mass of Br₂ instead of 160 gives 0.20 mol and Mr = 21, which matches no alkene.

questions.s: How many alkenes with the formula C₄H₈ exist if cis and trans isomers are counted separately?
questions.e: The structures are but-1-ene CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃, but-2-ene CH₃CH=CHCH₃ and 2-methylpropene (CH₃)₂C=CH₂. But-2-ene exists as cis and trans forms, so the total is 4. Answering 3 forgets the geometric isomers; cyclobutane is not an alkene, so 5 is too many.

questions.s: Ethene, CH₂=CH₂, is polymerised to make poly(ethene). What is the repeating unit of the polymer?
questions.e: In addition polymerisation the C=C bond opens and the monomers join end to end, so the repeating unit is the monomer with a single bond: –CH₂–CH₂–. –CH=CH– still keeps a double bond, which is lost in the reaction, and –CH₂–CH(CH₃)– is the unit of poly(propene).

questions.s: Poly(chloroethene), PVC, has the repeating unit –CH₂–CHCl–. What is its monomer?
questions.e: Put the double bond back between the two carbons of the repeating unit: CH₂=CHCl, chloroethene (vinyl chloride). CH₃CH₂Cl has no double bond and cannot undergo addition polymerisation; the other two have two Cl atoms per unit.

questions.s: Which of these alkanes has the highest boiling point?
questions.e: The three C₅H₁₂ isomers have equal Mr, but the unbranched pentane has the largest surface contact, so its London (dispersion) forces are strongest (about 36 °C, against 28 °C and 10 °C). Butane has a smaller Mr and boils near 0 °C. Branching lowers the boiling point, so 2,2-dimethylpropane is the lowest of the C₅ isomers.

questions.s: Which statement about ethene and ethane is correct?
o: Bromine water distinguishes ethene from ethane
Ethane adds H₂ when heated with a Ni catalyst
All eight atoms of ethane lie in one plane
questions.e: Ethene adds Br₂ and decolourises bromine water, while ethane does not react, so bromine water tells them apart. Only ethene is oxidised by acidified KMnO₄; ethane is already saturated and cannot add H₂. Ethane is tetrahedral at each carbon, so its atoms are not coplanar (ethene's six atoms are).

questions.s: 2-methylbutane, (CH₃)₂CHCH₂CH₃, reacts with chlorine in light. How many different monochlorinated products C₅H₁₁Cl can form (ignore stereoisomers)?
questions.e: The two CH₃ groups on C2 are equivalent, so the distinct H environments are: those two CH₃ groups, the CH on C2, the CH₂ on C3 and the CH₃ on C4. That is 4 environments and 4 monochloro products. Counting 5 treats the two equivalent methyl groups as different.

questions.s: Which compound belongs to the same homologous series as methane, CH₄?
questions.e: Methane is an alkane, CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, and C₃H₈ (propane) fits this formula with n = 3; it differs from CH₄ by two CH₂ units. C₂H₄ is an alkene, C₂H₂ an alkyne and C₆H₆ is benzene, so they are in different series.

questions.s: 0.25 mol of propyne, CH₃C≡CH, is converted completely into propane with H₂ over a nickel catalyst. What volume of H₂ is needed at STP? (molar volume 22.4 L/mol)
questions.e: A triple bond needs 2 mol H₂ per mole to become saturated: CH₃C≡CH + 2H₂ → CH₃CH₂CH₃. n(H₂) = 2 × 0.25 = 0.50 mol, and 0.50 × 22.4 = 11.2 L. 5.6 L uses only 1 mol H₂ per mol, which would stop at propene.

questions.s: Adding HCl to which alkene gives only one structural product?
questions.e: But-2-ene is symmetrical, so whichever double-bond carbon receives Cl the product is 2-chlorobutane. The other alkenes are unsymmetrical: propene can give 1- or 2-chloropropane, but-1-ene 1- or 2-chlorobutane, and pent-2-ene 2- or 3-chloropentane.

questions.s: 0.20 mol of a mixture of methane and ethene is passed through excess bromine water, and the mass of the bromine water increases by 1.4 g. What percentage of the mixture, by volume, is methane? (C = 12, H = 1)
questions.e: Only ethene is absorbed (it adds Br₂), so the mass gain is the ethene: 1.4/28 = 0.05 mol. Methane is 0.20 − 0.05 = 0.15 mol, and 0.15/0.20 = 75% by volume. 25% is the ethene share, not the methane share.

questions.s: Which statement about the benzene molecule, C₆H₆, is correct?
o: It has three C=C and three C–C bonds of different lengths
All six carbon–carbon bonds have the same length
It is puckered and non-planar, like cyclohexane
It decolourises bromine water by addition
questions.e: X-ray data show all six C–C bonds in benzene are equal (about 0.140 nm, between a single and a double bond) because the π electrons are delocalised around the planar ring. The alternating single/double (Kekulé) picture is wrong for that reason, and the delocalised ring resists addition, so benzene does not decolourise bromine water by reaction.

questions.s: Benzene reacts with liquid bromine in the presence of FeBr₃. What is the main organic product?
questions.e: FeBr₃ (formed from Fe and Br₂) catalyses electrophilic substitution: C₆H₆ + Br₂ → C₆H₅Br + HBr, giving bromobenzene. C₆H₆Br₂ and C₆H₆Br₆ would be addition products, which the stable aromatic ring does not form under these conditions.

questions.s: Benzene is nitrated by warming it to about 55 °C with a mixture of concentrated nitric acid and concentrated sulfuric acid. What is the role of the sulfuric acid?
questions.e: Concentrated H₂SO₄ protonates HNO₃ to form the NO₂⁺ electrophile and absorbs the water formed, and it is not used up, so it acts as a catalyst (and dehydrating agent). The nitrogen in nitrobenzene, C₆H₅NO₂, comes from HNO₃, not from the sulfuric acid.

questions.s: How many isomers with the formula C₈H₁₀ contain a benzene ring?
questions.e: Two methyl groups on the ring give three dimethylbenzenes: 1,2-, 1,3- and 1,4-. A single ethyl group gives ethylbenzene, C₆H₅CH₂CH₃. The total is 4; answering 3 forgets ethylbenzene.

questions.s: Which reagent can distinguish benzene from methylbenzene (toluene)?
questions.e: The ring activates the CH₃ side chain of methylbenzene, which is oxidised by acidified KMnO₄ (to benzoic acid), so the purple colour fades; benzene leaves it purple. With bromine water both liquids simply extract the bromine into an orange upper layer, so it does not tell them apart.

questions.s: Phenylethene (styrene), C₆H₅CH=CH₂, is hydrogenated completely over a nickel catalyst to give ethylcyclohexane. How many moles of H₂ react with 1 mol of styrene?
questions.e: The side-chain C=C needs 1 mol H₂ and the benzene ring needs 3 mol H₂ to become a cyclohexane ring, so 4 mol in total (C₈H₈ → C₈H₁₆). Answering 1 treats the ring as inert; answering 3 counts only the ring.

questions.s: Which of the following compounds is aromatic?
questions.e: Aromatic compounds contain a benzene ring; phenol is a benzene ring carrying an –OH group. Cyclohexane is a saturated ring with no delocalised electrons, and hexane and buta-1,3-diene are open-chain compounds.

questions.s: In methylbenzene, C₆H₅CH₃, what is the maximum number of atoms that can lie in the same plane?
questions.e: The benzene ring is planar, so its 6 C atoms, its 5 H atoms and the methyl carbon (which replaces a ring H) are coplanar: 12 atoms. The methyl carbon is tetrahedral, but rotation can bring one of its three H atoms into the ring plane, giving 13. 15 wrongly puts all three methyl H atoms in the plane.

questions.s: A small piece of sodium is dropped into ethanol. Which gas is given off?
questions.e: Sodium replaces the H of the –OH group: 2CH₃CH₂OH + 2Na → 2CH₃CH₂ONa + H₂. The reaction is gentler than with water because the O–H bond in ethanol is less polar. No carbon dioxide or ethene is formed.

questions.s: 0.40 mol of ethanol reacts with excess sodium. What volume of hydrogen is produced at STP? (molar volume 22.4 L/mol)
questions.e: 2CH₃CH₂OH + 2Na → 2CH₃CH₂ONa + H₂, so n(H₂) = 0.40/2 = 0.20 mol and V = 0.20 × 22.4 = 4.48 L. 8.96 L ignores the 2 : 1 ratio and assumes one H₂ per ethanol molecule.

questions.s: 0.10 mol of an alcohol reacts with excess sodium to give 2.24 L of H₂ at STP. Which could the alcohol be?
questions.e: n(H₂) = 2.24/22.4 = 0.10 mol. Each –OH releases ½ H₂, so 0.10 mol alcohol giving 0.10 mol H₂ means 2 –OH groups per molecule, as in ethane-1,2-diol. A mono-alcohol would give only 0.05 mol H₂, and propane-1,2,3-triol (glycerol) would give 0.15 mol.

questions.s: Ethanol vapour mixed with air is passed over heated copper. What is the main organic product?
questions.e: Copper catalyses the oxidation 2CH₃CH₂OH + O₂ → 2CH₃CHO + 2H₂O, giving ethanal (acetaldehyde); the copper turns black (CuO) and then red again. Acetic acid would need further oxidation, for example by acidified KMnO₄ or K₂Cr₂O₇.

questions.s: Ethanol is heated with concentrated sulfuric acid at 170 °C. What is the main organic product?
questions.e: At 170 °C, concentrated H₂SO₄ removes H₂O from within each molecule (elimination): CH₃CH₂OH → CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O. Diethyl ether, CH₃CH₂OCH₂CH₃, is the main product at the lower temperature of about 140 °C, when water is removed between two molecules.

questions.s: Which alcohol is oxidised by acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ to a ketone?
questions.e: Propan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol; its C–OH carbon has one H, so oxidation gives propanone, CH₃COCH₃. Primary alcohols such as propan-1-ol and methanol give aldehydes and then acids. The tertiary alcohol (CH₃)₃COH has no H on the C–OH carbon and resists oxidation.

questions.s: Which alcohol cannot form an alkene by elimination of water?
questions.e: Elimination removes the –OH and an H atom from the neighbouring carbon. In (CH₃)₃CCH₂OH the neighbouring carbon is C(CH₃)₃, which has no H atom, so no C=C can form. (CH₃)₃COH cannot be oxidised easily, but its neighbouring CH₃ groups do have H atoms, so it dehydrates readily to 2-methylpropene.

questions.s: Ethanol, CH₃CH₂OH, boils at 78 °C, but dimethyl ether, CH₃OCH₃, which has the same molar mass, boils at −24 °C. What is the main reason?
o: Ethanol has a larger relative molecular mass
Dimethyl ether has weaker C–O covalent bonds
Ethanol molecules hydrogen-bond to each other
Ethanol molecules are held by ionic bonds
questions.e: Ethanol has an O–H group, so its molecules form hydrogen bonds with one another, which need extra energy to break on boiling. Dimethyl ether has no H on oxygen and only weaker dipole and dispersion forces. Both have Mr = 46, and boiling breaks intermolecular forces, not covalent bonds.

questions.s: Which functional group do all alcohols contain?
questions.e: Alcohols contain the hydroxyl group –OH bonded to a saturated carbon, as in CH₃CH₂OH. –CHO is the aldehyde group, –COOH the carboxyl group and –COO– the ester linkage.

questions.s: Which statement about phenol, C₆H₅OH, is correct?
o: It is a weaker acid than H₂CO₃
It does not react with NaOH solution
It releases CO₂ from NaHCO₃ solution
It gives a red precipitate with FeCl₃
questions.e: Phenol is weakly acidic: it dissolves in NaOH to form C₆H₅ONa, but it is weaker than carbonic acid, so it cannot release CO₂ from NaHCO₃ (CO₂ bubbled into sodium phenoxide solution even regenerates phenol). With FeCl₃ phenol gives a violet colour, not a red precipitate.

questions.s: A dilute solution of phenol is added to excess bromine water. What is observed?
o: Bubbles of gas are given off
questions.e: The –OH group activates the ring, so phenol is substituted at three positions at once without a catalyst, giving a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol and HBr. The violet (purple) colour is the test with FeCl₃, and a silver mirror is the test for an aldehyde group.

questions.s: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH(OH)CH₃?
questions.e: The chain has three carbons and the –OH group is on the middle carbon, C2, so the name is propan-2-ol (isopropyl alcohol). Propan-1-ol is CH₃CH₂CH₂OH, and propanone is the ketone CH₃COCH₃ formed when propan-2-ol is oxidised.

questions.s: How many alcohols have the molecular formula C₄H₁₀O?
questions.e: The four alcohols are butan-1-ol, butan-2-ol, 2-methylpropan-1-ol and 2-methylpropan-2-ol. The value 7 also counts the three ethers with this formula (CH₃OCH₂CH₂CH₃, CH₃OCH(CH₃)₂ and CH₃CH₂OCH₂CH₃), which are not alcohols.

questions.s: How are ethanol, CH₃CH₂OH, and methoxymethane, CH₃OCH₃, related?
questions.e: Both have the formula C₂H₆O but contain different functional groups (–OH and –O–), so they are structural isomers of the functional-group type. Homologues differ by CH₂ units and have the same functional group, and cis-trans isomerism needs a C=C bond.

questions.s: 4.6 g of ethanol, C₂H₅OH, burns completely in oxygen. What mass of water is formed? (H = 1, C = 12, O = 16)
questions.e: n(C₂H₅OH) = 4.6/46 = 0.10 mol. Each molecule has 6 H atoms, which form 3 H₂O, so n(H₂O) = 0.30 mol and the mass is 0.30 × 18 = 5.4 g. 8.8 g is the mass of CO₂ (0.20 mol × 44), not of water.

questions.s: In an old breath test, ethanol is passed into acidified potassium dichromate, which turns from orange to green. Which statement is correct?
o: Ethanol is reduced; Cr goes from +6 to +3
Ethanol is oxidised; Cr goes from +6 to +3
Ethanol is oxidised; Cr goes from +3 to +6
Ethanol is reduced; Cr goes from +3 to +6
questions.e: Orange Cr₂O₇²⁻ contains Cr(+6) and is reduced to green Cr³⁺ (+3). Ethanol is the reducing agent and is itself oxidised, to ethanal and then acetic acid. Saying ethanol is reduced confuses the oxidising agent with the reducing agent.

questions.s: 6.0 g of a saturated alcohol with one –OH group reacts with excess sodium to give 1.12 L of H₂ at STP. What is the formula of the alcohol? (H = 1, C = 12, O = 16)
questions.e: n(H₂) = 1.12/22.4 = 0.050 mol, and 2 mol of a mono-alcohol give 1 mol H₂, so n(alcohol) = 0.10 mol. Mr = 6.0/0.10 = 60, and CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH has Mr = 14n + 18 = 60, so n = 3: C₃H₇OH. Taking n(alcohol) = n(H₂) = 0.05 mol gives Mr = 120, which matches none of the options.

questions.s: Which of the following compounds is an aldehyde?
questions.e: Aldehydes contain the –CHO group, a C=O at the end of a chain with an H on the same carbon; CH₃CH₂CHO is propanal. CH₃COCH₃ has its C=O between two carbons, so it is a ketone (propanone). CH₃COOH is a carboxylic acid and CH₃CH₂OH an alcohol.

questions.s: Which compound forms a silver mirror when warmed with Tollens' reagent (ammoniacal silver nitrate)?
questions.e: The silver mirror test detects the –CHO group, which reduces [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺ to metallic Ag while being oxidised. Methanal, HCHO, is an aldehyde. Propanone is a ketone, and ethanol and methyl ethanoate have no –CHO group, so none of them gives a mirror.

questions.s: An aldehyde is boiled with freshly prepared Cu(OH)₂ suspension in excess NaOH, and a brick-red precipitate forms. What is the precipitate?
questions.e: The aldehyde reduces copper(II) to copper(I), giving brick-red copper(I) oxide, Cu₂O; the aldehyde is oxidised to a carboxylate. Cu(OH)₂ is the blue starting material, CuO is black, and metallic copper is not formed in this test.

questions.s: 4.4 g of ethanal, CH₃CHO, reacts completely with excess Tollens' reagent. What mass of silver is deposited? (H = 1, C = 12, O = 16, Ag = 108)
questions.e: n(CH₃CHO) = 4.4/44 = 0.10 mol. Each –CHO group gives 2 Ag (RCHO is oxidised to RCOO⁻ as 2 Ag⁺ are reduced), so n(Ag) = 0.20 mol and m = 0.20 × 108 = 21.6 g. 43.2 g uses the 1 : 4 ratio that applies only to methanal, HCHO, which behaves as if it had two –CHO groups.

questions.s: Ethanal reacts with hydrogen in the presence of a nickel catalyst. Which statement is correct?
o: Ethanal is reduced to acetic acid
questions.e: H₂ adds across the C=O bond: CH₃CHO + H₂ → CH₃CH₂OH. Gaining hydrogen is reduction (it is also an addition reaction). Acetic acid would come from oxidation of ethanal, not from reaction with hydrogen.

questions.s: Which reagent can be used to distinguish propanal, CH₃CH₂CHO, from propanone, CH₃COCH₃?
questions.e: Propanal has an aldehyde –CHO group and gives a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent; propanone is a ketone and does not. Neither compound is acidic, so litmus and NaOH show no difference, and neither has an O–H group to react with sodium.

questions.s: What is the functional group of acetic acid (ethanoic acid), CH₃COOH?
questions.e: Carboxylic acids contain the carboxyl group –COOH, in which a C=O and an –OH are on the same carbon. That combination behaves differently from a separate –OH (alcohol) or C=O, for example it is acidic enough to react with carbonates.

questions.s: Which observation shows that acetic acid is a stronger acid than carbonic acid?
o: It forms CO₂ with NaHCO₃ solution
It turns blue litmus paper red
It reacts with sodium metal to give H₂ gas
questions.e: CH₃COOH + NaHCO₃ → CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂: a stronger acid displaces a weaker acid from its salt. Turning litmus red only shows that it is an acid, and sodium also gives H₂ with water and ethanol, which are not acids stronger than carbonic acid.

questions.s: Acetic acid is esterified with ethanol labelled with oxygen-18, CH₃CH₂¹⁸OH, using concentrated sulfuric acid. Where is the ¹⁸O found afterwards?
questions.e: In esterification the acid loses its –OH and the alcohol loses only the H of its –OH: CH₃CO–OH + H–¹⁸OCH₂CH₃ → CH₃CO¹⁸OCH₂CH₃ + H₂O. So the labelled oxygen stays in the ester. Thinking the alcohol loses its whole –OH group would put ¹⁸O in the water.

questions.s: What is the IUPAC name of the ester CH₃COOCH₂CH₃?
questions.e: The ester is named alkyl group first, then the acid part with -oate. The CH₃CO– part comes from ethanoic acid and the –CH₂CH₃ on the oxygen from ethanol, so it is ethyl ethanoate (ethyl acetate). Methyl propanoate would be CH₃CH₂COOCH₃, an isomer with the same formula C₄H₈O₂.

questions.s: Which ester also gives a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent?
questions.e: Methanoate (formate) esters, HCOOR, contain an H–C=O unit that behaves like an aldehyde group, so ethyl methanoate reduces Tollens' reagent. In the other esters the C=O carbon is bonded to an alkyl group, not to H, so there is no aldehyde-like hydrogen.

questions.s: Ethyl ethanoate is boiled with sodium hydroxide solution until hydrolysis is complete. What are the organic products?
questions.e: CH₃COOCH₂CH₃ + NaOH → CH₃COONa + CH₃CH₂OH. In alkali the acid part ends up as its sodium salt, while the alcohol is released as ethanol; ethanol is far too weak an acid to form CH₃CH₂ONa in water. CH₃CH₂COONa and CH₃OH would come from the isomer methyl propanoate.

questions.s: When ethyl ethanoate is made from acetic acid and ethanol, the ester is distilled off as it forms. Why does this increase the yield?
o: It shifts the equilibrium towards the ester
It increases the rate constant of the reaction
It stops the acid catalyst being used up
It prevents the ethanol being oxidised
questions.e: Esterification is reversible: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. Removing a product lowers its concentration, so by Le Chatelier's principle the equilibrium shifts to the right. Removing product does not change the rate constant, and the catalyst is not consumed anyway.

questions.s: In the laboratory preparation of ethyl ethanoate, the vapour is condensed onto the surface of saturated Na₂CO₃ solution. What is one purpose of this solution?
questions.e: Saturated Na₂CO₃ solution reacts with acetic acid that distils over, dissolves ethanol, and lowers the solubility of the ester, which floats as an oily upper layer. It is far too weakly basic to hydrolyse much ester in the short contact time, and the catalyst is the concentrated H₂SO₄ in the reaction flask.

questions.s: Which order of acid strength is correct?
questions.e: Acetic acid releases CO₂ from carbonates, so it is stronger than carbonic acid. Carbonic acid is stronger than phenol, since CO₂ passed into sodium phenoxide solution turns it cloudy with phenol. The order CH₃COOH > H₂CO₃ > C₆H₅OH follows; putting phenol above carbonic acid is the common error.

questions.s: How many esters have the molecular formula C₄H₈O₂?
questions.e: They are HCOOCH₂CH₂CH₃ (propyl methanoate), HCOOCH(CH₃)₂ (1-methylethyl methanoate), CH₃COOCH₂CH₃ (ethyl ethanoate) and CH₃CH₂COOCH₃ (methyl propanoate): 4 esters. 6 also counts the two carboxylic acids with this formula, butanoic acid and 2-methylpropanoic acid, which are not esters.

questions.s: 6.0 g of acetic acid is heated with excess ethanol and concentrated sulfuric acid. The yield of ethyl ethanoate is 50%. What mass of ester is obtained? (H = 1, C = 12, O = 16)
questions.e: n(CH₃COOH) = 6.0/60 = 0.10 mol, which could give 0.10 mol of CH₃COOC₂H₅ (Mr = 88), that is 8.8 g at 100%. At 50% yield the mass is 4.4 g. 8.8 g forgets the yield, and 3.0 g wrongly takes half the mass of the acid.

questions.s: Which formula represents propanone (acetone)?
questions.e: Propanone is a three-carbon ketone with the C=O group on the middle carbon: CH₃COCH₃. CH₃CH₂CHO is its isomer propanal, an aldehyde, and the other two contain two oxygen atoms (an acid and an ester).

questions.s: Ethanal, CH₃CHO, is converted into acetic acid, CH₃COOH, using oxygen and a catalyst. What type of reaction is this?
questions.e: The molecule gains an oxygen atom (2CH₃CHO + O₂ → 2CH₃COOH), so the aldehyde is oxidised. Reduction of ethanal would give ethanol. No water is added or removed, so it is neither hydrolysis nor dehydration.

questions.s: A solution of methanal (formalin) is used to preserve biological specimens. Why is it effective?
questions.e: Methanal reacts with proteins and denatures them irreversibly, which kills microorganisms and stops the tissue decaying. It is not a strong acid and does not hydrolyse fats or dissolve cellulose. For the same reason it is toxic and must not be used on food.

questions.s: Compound X, C₃H₆O, contains a C=O group, does not react with sodium and does not give a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent. What is X?
questions.e: A C=O compound that fails the silver mirror test is a ketone, not an aldehyde, so X is propanone, CH₃COCH₃. Propanal gives a silver mirror; CH₂=CHCH₂OH has an –OH group that reacts with sodium, and CH₂=CHOCH₃ has no C=O group.

questions.s: Why does the hydrolysis of an ester with NaOH solution go to completion, while hydrolysis with dilute acid does not?
o: NaOH acts only as a catalyst
The alcohol formed boils off at once
The acid formed is removed as its salt
The ester reacts faster in base than in acid
questions.e: In alkali the carboxylic acid is converted at once into its carboxylate ion (RCOO⁻), which cannot react with the alcohol, so the reverse reaction (esterification) cannot happen. In acid the reaction is an equilibrium. NaOH is consumed, so it is a reactant rather than a catalyst, and speed alone cannot change the position of an equilibrium.

questions.s: Vinegar can remove kettle scale, which is mainly CaCO₃. Why?
o: acetic acid is a strong oxidising agent
acetic acid is a strong reducing agent
acetic acid forms an ester with CaCO₃
acetic acid is stronger than carbonic acid
questions.e: 2CH₃COOH + CaCO₃ → (CH₃COO)₂Ca + H₂O + CO₂. A stronger acid displaces the weaker carbonic acid, which decomposes to CO₂ and water, and calcium acetate is soluble. No redox reaction or esterification takes place; esters form from acids and alcohols.

questions.s: Phenyl ethanoate, CH₃COOC₆H₅, is heated with excess NaOH solution until no ester remains. How many moles of NaOH react with 1 mol of the ester?
questions.e: Hydrolysis gives CH₃COOH and phenol, C₆H₅OH, and in excess NaOH both are acidic enough to be neutralised: CH₃COOC₆H₅ + 2NaOH → CH₃COONa + C₆H₅ONa + H₂O. So 2 mol NaOH are used. Answering 1 treats it like an ester of an ordinary alcohol, whose alcohol product does not react with NaOH.

questions.s: What volume of 0.10 mol/L NaOH solution exactly neutralises 0.60 g of acetic acid? (H = 1, C = 12, O = 16)
questions.e: n(CH₃COOH) = 0.60/60 = 0.010 mol, and CH₃COOH + NaOH → CH₃COONa + H₂O is 1 : 1, so n(NaOH) = 0.010 mol. V = 0.010/0.10 = 0.10 L = 100 mL. 200 mL wrongly assumes a 1 : 2 ratio; only the H of –COOH is acidic, not the H atoms of CH₃.

questions.s: Which molecule contains a chiral carbon atom (a carbon bonded to four different groups)?
questions.e: In lactic acid, CH₃CH(OH)COOH, the middle carbon carries H, CH₃, OH and COOH, four different groups, so it is chiral and the molecule has two mirror-image forms. In propan-2-ol the C–OH carbon carries two identical CH₃ groups, and the other molecules have at least two H atoms on every carbon.

questions.s: What is the IUPAC name of CH₂=C(CH₃)CH₂CH₃?
questions.e: The longest chain containing the C=C has 4 carbons. Numbering from the CH₂= end gives the double bond the lowest locant (1) and puts the methyl on C2: 2-methylbut-1-ene. '3-methylbut-3-ene' numbers from the wrong end, and 2-methylbut-2-ene is (CH₃)₂C=CHCH₃, a different isomer.

questions.s: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂COOH?
questions.e: The chain has three carbons including the carboxyl carbon, and the –COOH group gives the ending -oic acid: propanoic acid. Ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH, has only two carbons; propanal is the aldehyde CH₃CH₂CHO.

questions.s: What is the IUPAC name of CH≡CCH₂CH₃?
questions.e: There are 4 carbons with a triple bond (ending -yne) between C1 and C2 when numbered from the CH≡ end, giving but-1-yne. Numbering from the other end would give the higher locant 3, which is not allowed. But-2-yne is CH₃C≡CCH₃, and '-ene' would mean a double bond.

questions.s: What is the IUPAC name of (CH₃)₂CHCH₂OH?
questions.e: The longest chain containing the C–OH carbon is three carbons: HOCH₂–CH(CH₃)–CH₃. Numbering from the –OH end puts the OH on C1 and the methyl on C2, so it is 2-methylpropan-1-ol. 2-Methylpropan-2-ol is (CH₃)₃COH, with the –OH on the branched carbon.

questions.s: Ethene is bubbled into a solution of chlorine in an inert solvent. What is the name of the organic product?
questions.e: Cl₂ adds across the C=C bond, one Cl atom to each carbon: CH₂=CH₂ + Cl₂ → CH₂ClCH₂Cl, which is 1,2-dichloroethane. 1,1-Dichloroethane would need both Cl atoms on the same carbon, which addition cannot give, and chloroethane would come from adding HCl.

questions.s: But-1-ene, CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃, and but-2-ene, CH₃CH=CHCH₃, are best described as
questions.e: Both have the same unbranched carbon chain and the same functional group (C=C); only the position of the double bond differs, so they are position isomers. Cis-trans isomers differ only in spatial arrangement about the double bond, as in cis- and trans-but-2-ene.

questions.s: Which pair of compounds are isomers of each other?
questions.e: Acetic acid and methyl methanoate both have the molecular formula C₂H₄O₂ but different structures, so they are isomers. Ethanol (C₂H₆O) and ethanal (C₂H₄O) have different formulas, as do ethene and ethyne. CH₄ and C₂H₆ are homologues, not isomers.

questions.s: Which pair of compounds belong to the same homologous series?
questions.e: Methanol and ethanol are both alcohols with one –OH group, and they differ by one CH₂ unit, so they are homologues. CH₃OCH₃ is an ether and CH₃COCH₃ a ketone, so those pairs contain different functional groups. O₂ and O₃ are allotropes.

questions.s: The open-chain form of glucose is CH₂OH(CHOH)₄CHO. How many chiral carbon atoms does it contain?
questions.e: The four CHOH carbons (C2 to C5) each carry H, OH and two different carbon-containing groups, so all four are chiral. C1 (the CHO carbon) has only three groups, with a double bond to O, and C6 (CH₂OH) carries two H atoms, so neither is chiral. Answering 5 wrongly includes one of these end carbons.

questions.s: How many structural isomers have the formula C₃H₆Cl₂?
questions.e: On a three-carbon chain the two Cl atoms can be placed 1,1 (CHCl₂CH₂CH₃), 1,2 (CH₂ClCHClCH₃), 1,3 (CH₂ClCH₂CH₂Cl) or 2,2 (CH₃CCl₂CH₃): 4 isomers. 3,3 and 2,3 are the same as 1,1 and 1,2 numbered from the other end, so counting them gives too many.

questions.s: Bromoethane, CH₃CH₂Br, is heated with aqueous sodium hydroxide. What are the main organic product and the type of reaction?
questions.e: In aqueous NaOH the OH⁻ replaces the Br atom: CH₃CH₂Br + NaOH → CH₃CH₂OH + NaBr, a substitution (hydrolysis). Elimination to ethene needs NaOH dissolved in ethanol, heated, instead of water.

questions.s: Bromoethane is heated under reflux with a concentrated solution of NaOH in ethanol. What are the main organic product and the type of reaction?
questions.e: In ethanolic NaOH, HBr is removed from neighbouring carbons: CH₃CH₂Br + NaOH → CH₂=CH₂ + NaBr + H₂O, so the product is ethene and the reaction is elimination. Substitution to ethanol is the main reaction in aqueous NaOH, so the solvent decides which path dominates.

questions.s: Which of the following reactions is a substitution reaction?
questions.e: In the nitration of benzene an H atom on the ring is replaced by an –NO₂ group, which is substitution. The bromine reaction with ethene is addition, the ethanol reaction is elimination (dehydration), and the last one is addition polymerisation.

questions.s: Ethanol reacts with acetic acid to form ethyl ethanoate and water. In most school classifications, which type of reaction is this?
questions.e: In esterification the –OH of the acid is replaced by the –OCH₂CH₃ group of the alcohol (and water is released), so it is classed as a substitution, also called a condensation. Nothing adds across a multiple bond and no new multiple bond forms, so it is neither addition nor elimination, and it is not a redox reaction.

questions.s: Which polymer is made by condensation polymerisation?
questions.e: Nylon-6,6 forms from hexanedioic acid and hexane-1,6-diamine; each amide link formed releases a molecule of water, which is the mark of condensation polymerisation. The other three are made by addition polymerisation of C=C monomers, with no small molecule lost.

questions.s: Poly(tetrafluoroethene), PTFE, is used to coat non-stick pans. What is its monomer?
questions.e: Tetrafluoroethene is CF₂=CF₂, with four F atoms around a C=C bond; addition polymerisation gives –[CF₂–CF₂]ₙ–. CF₃CF₃ is saturated, so it cannot polymerise by addition, and the other two monomers contain only two F atoms.

questions.s: What is the repeating unit of poly(propene), made from propene CH₂=CHCH₃?
questions.e: Only the two carbons of the C=C bond join the chain; the CH₃ group stays as a side branch, giving –CH₂–CH(CH₃)–. Writing –CH₂–CH₂–CH₂– wrongly puts all three carbons into the main chain, and the double bond disappears on polymerisation.

questions.s: A polyester has the repeating unit –OC–C₆H₄–COO–CH₂CH₂–O–, where the two carbonyl groups are on opposite (1,4) positions of the ring. Which pair of monomers is it made from?
questions.e: Each ester link –CO–O– is formed from a –COOH and an –OH, with loss of water. So the unit comes from benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid (two –COOH) and ethane-1,2-diol (two –OH); both monomers must be bifunctional to build a chain. Benzoic acid has only one –COOH, and ethene cannot form ester links.

questions.s: A sample of poly(ethene) has an average relative molecular mass of 56 000. What is the average number of ethene units in each chain? (C = 12, H = 1)
questions.e: The repeating unit –CH₂–CH₂– has Mr = 28, so n = 56 000/28 = 2000. Dividing by 14 (one CH₂ group) instead of 28 gives 4000, which counts CH₂ groups rather than monomer units.

questions.s: Discarded poly(ethene) bags cause long-lasting 'white pollution'. Which property of poly(ethene) is mainly responsible?
questions.e: Poly(ethene) is a saturated, chemically inert chain that microorganisms break down extremely slowly, so it persists for decades. It is insoluble in water, contains no chlorine, and is an electrical insulator.

questions.s: Which compound can form a polymer by addition polymerisation?
questions.e: Addition polymerisation needs a C=C bond in the monomer; propenoic acid (acrylic acid) CH₂=CHCOOH has one and gives poly(propenoic acid). Ethanol, acetic acid and ethane are saturated, so they cannot open a double bond to link up.

questions.s: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH(CH₃)CH(CH₂CH₃)CH₃?
questions.e: The longest chain runs through the ethyl group: CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–CH₃, five carbons. Numbering from the left gives methyl groups on C2 and C3, so the name is 2,3-dimethylpentane. Any 'butane' name has missed the longer chain, and 3,4 uses higher locants than necessary.

questions.s: Which molecular formula could belong to a compound containing a benzene ring?
questions.e: A benzene ring needs 4 degrees of unsaturation (one ring plus three double bonds). For C₇H₈: (2 × 7 + 2 − 8)/2 = 4, which fits methylbenzene. C₆H₁₂ and C₅H₁₀ have 1 and C₆H₁₀ has 2, too few for a benzene ring.

questions.s: How many structural isomers have the formula C₄H₉Cl?
questions.e: Butane gives 1-chlorobutane and 2-chlorobutane, and 2-methylpropane gives 1-chloro-2-methylpropane and 2-chloro-2-methylpropane: 4 isomers. This matches the four different C₄H₉ groups. Answering 2 forgets the branched chain.

questions.s: Glucose and fructose are isomers. What is their molecular formula?
questions.e: Both are monosaccharides with formula C₆H₁₂O₆: glucose has an aldehyde group and fructose a ketone group. C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ is a disaccharide such as sucrose, and C₆H₁₀O₅ is the repeating unit of starch and cellulose.

questions.s: Which reagent is used to test for starch?
questions.e: Iodine (I₂ in KI solution) turns blue-black with starch. Tollens' reagent tests for –CHO groups, biuret reagent for proteins (peptide bonds), and FeCl₃ for phenols.

questions.s: Which of these carbohydrates does not reduce Tollens' reagent?
questions.e: Sucrose is a non-reducing sugar: glucose and fructose are joined through both of their reducing (carbonyl) carbons, so no free aldehyde group remains. Glucose, maltose and lactose each keep a free reducing group and give a silver mirror. Sucrose reacts only after it has been hydrolysed.

questions.s: Sucrose is hydrolysed completely by warming it with dilute acid. What are the products?
questions.e: C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ + H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ (glucose) + C₆H₁₂O₆ (fructose). Glucose alone is the product from maltose, starch or cellulose, and glucose plus galactose comes from lactose.

questions.s: Which linkage joins amino acids together in a protein chain?
questions.e: The –COOH of one amino acid condenses with the –NH₂ of the next, losing water and forming a peptide (amide) bond, –CO–NH–. Ester links –COO– join fatty acids to glycerol in fats, not amino acids in proteins.

questions.s: Which treatment of an egg-white (protein) solution produces a precipitate that redissolves when water is added?
questions.e: A concentrated solution of a light-metal salt such as (NH₄)₂SO₄ 'salts out' the protein: it only lowers its solubility, so the protein redissolves in water and stays active. Heavy-metal ions (Cu²⁺), heat and methanal denature the protein, which is irreversible.

questions.s: Concentrated nitric acid is accidentally spilt on the skin. What colour does the skin turn?
questions.e: Proteins containing benzene rings react with concentrated HNO₃ (the xanthoproteic reaction) to give a yellow colour. Violet is the colour of the biuret test with Cu²⁺ in alkali, and blue-black is the iodine test for starch.

questions.s: Glycine, H₂NCH₂COOH, reacts with both hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide solution. Why?
questions.e: The basic amino group –NH₂ accepts H⁺ from HCl, and the acidic carboxyl group –COOH gives H⁺ to OH⁻, so glycine is amphoteric. It has only one –COOH, and as a single amino acid it has no peptide bond.

questions.s: A mixture of glycine and alanine is allowed to form dipeptides. How many different dipeptides are possible?
questions.e: Each dipeptide has an N-terminal and a C-terminal residue, so the order matters: Gly–Gly, Ala–Ala, Gly–Ala and Ala–Gly give 4. Answering 3 treats Gly–Ala and Ala–Gly as the same, but they are different compounds because the free –NH₂ and –COOH are on different residues.

questions.s: Fats and oils are esters of long-chain fatty acids with which alcohol?
questions.e: Fats and oils are triglycerides: each glycerol molecule (propane-1,2,3-triol, three –OH groups) is esterified by three fatty-acid molecules. Ethanol and methanol have only one –OH, and ethylene glycol has two.

questions.s: A fat is boiled with sodium hydroxide solution until it is completely saponified. What are the products?
questions.e: Alkaline hydrolysis of a triglyceride gives glycerol and the sodium salts of the fatty acids, which are soap: for example (C₁₇H₃₅COO)₃C₃H₅ + 3NaOH → 3C₁₇H₃₅COONa + C₃H₅(OH)₃. In alkali the acids end up as salts, not free acids, and the alcohol released is glycerol, not ethanol.

questions.s: How are liquid vegetable oils converted into solid fats for margarine?
o: adding H₂ over a Ni catalyst
questions.e: Vegetable oils contain many C=C bonds in their fatty-acid chains. Adding hydrogen over nickel saturates some of them, which straightens the chains, lets them pack better and raises the melting point. Hot NaOH would hydrolyse the oil into soap and glycerol instead.

questions.s: Triolein (Mr = 884) is an oil with three C=C bonds per molecule. What mass of bromine adds to 8.84 g of triolein? (Br = 80)
questions.e: n(triolein) = 8.84/884 = 0.010 mol. Each C=C adds one Br₂, so n(Br₂) = 3 × 0.010 = 0.030 mol, and 0.030 × 160 = 4.8 g. 1.6 g counts only one C=C per molecule, and 9.6 g counts 6 Br₂ per molecule.

questions.s: What mass of CO₂ forms when 18 g of glucose, C₆H₁₂O₆, is completely oxidised in respiration? (H = 1, C = 12, O = 16)
questions.e: n(C₆H₁₂O₆) = 18/180 = 0.10 mol. C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O, so n(CO₂) = 0.60 mol and m = 0.60 × 44 = 26.4 g. 4.4 g forgets that each glucose molecule gives 6 CO₂.

questions.s: Starch and cellulose are both written (C₆H₁₀O₅)ₙ. Which statement is correct?
o: They are isomers of each other
Both are hydrolysed finally to glucose
Humans can digest both of them
questions.e: Both are polymers of glucose units, so complete hydrolysis of either gives glucose. They are not isomers because n differs (and so the molecular formulas differ). Only starch gives the blue-black iodine test, and humans lack the enzyme to digest cellulose.

questions.s: In the absence of air, yeast converts glucose into which products?
questions.e: Fermentation: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂, catalysed by yeast enzymes. Acetic acid forms only later if ethanol is oxidised by bacteria in air, and no oxygen is produced.

questions.s: Which element is present in all proteins but not in carbohydrates or fats?
questions.e: Proteins are built from amino acids, which contain an –NH₂ group, so every protein contains nitrogen (and many contain sulfur). Carbohydrates and fats contain only C, H and O.

questions.s: Which simple test distinguishes a wool thread from a cotton thread?
o: burn: wool smells of burnt hair
questions.e: Wool is a protein; when burned it gives the smell of burnt hair or feathers, while cotton (cellulose) smells like burnt paper. Cellulose does not give the starch–iodine colour, neither fibre dissolves in water, and neither is acidic enough to fizz with NaHCO₃.

questions.s: An enzyme-catalysed reaction in water slows sharply when the temperature is raised from 37 °C to 70 °C. What is the main reason?
questions.e: Enzymes are proteins; at high temperature their folded shape is destroyed (denaturation), so the active site no longer fits the substrate. Temperature does not raise the activation energy; a higher temperature alone would speed up an uncatalysed reaction.

questions.s: A mixture of 0.10 mol glucose and 0.10 mol sucrose is warmed with excess Tollens' reagent without any prior hydrolysis. What mass of silver is deposited? (Ag = 108)
questions.e: Only glucose has a free aldehyde group; sucrose is non-reducing until hydrolysed. Each –CHO gives 2 Ag, so n(Ag) = 2 × 0.10 = 0.20 mol and m = 0.20 × 108 = 21.6 g. 43.2 g wrongly lets sucrose react as well.

questions.s: Which molecular formula fits the general formula of the alkenes?
questions.e: Alkenes with one C=C bond have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ; with n = 4 this gives C₄H₈ (for example but-1-ene). C₃H₈ is an alkane (CₙH₂ₙ₊₂), C₄H₆ fits an alkyne or diene (CₙH₂ₙ₋₂), and C₆H₆ is benzene.

questions.s: What is the shape of a methane molecule, CH₄?
questions.e: The four C–H bonding pairs repel equally and point to the corners of a regular tetrahedron, with H–C–H angles of 109.5°. A flat square drawing on paper is only a convenience; it does not show the real 3-D shape.

questions.s: What is the main component of natural gas?
questions.e: Natural gas is mostly methane, CH₄, with smaller amounts of ethane and propane. Ethene is not a significant component; it is made by cracking larger alkanes.

questions.s: Which gas is released naturally by plants, is used to ripen fruit, and is the monomer of poly(ethene)?
questions.e: Ethene, CH₂=CH₂, acts as a plant hormone that speeds up ripening, and its C=C bond lets it undergo addition polymerisation to poly(ethene). Methane and propane are saturated, so they cannot polymerise this way.

questions.s: Which reagent can be used to distinguish ethene from methane?
questions.e: Ethene's C=C bond is oxidised by acidified KMnO₄, so the purple colour fades, while methane does not react. However, KMnO₄ is not used to remove ethene from methane, because it oxidises ethene to CO₂, a new impurity. Neither gas reacts with NaOH, limewater or water.

questions.s: Benzene is heated with excess hydrogen in the presence of a nickel catalyst. What is the product?
questions.e: C₆H₆ + 3H₂ → C₆H₁₂: the ring is kept, but all of its unsaturation is removed, giving cyclohexane. Hexane, C₆H₁₄, would need the ring to break, which does not happen. With excess H₂ the reaction does not stop at cyclohexene or cyclohexadiene.

questions.s: Ethanol is warmed with excess acidified potassium manganate(VII) solution. What is the final organic product?
questions.e: A primary alcohol is oxidised first to the aldehyde and then, with an excess of a strong oxidising agent, to the carboxylic acid: CH₃CH₂OH → CH₃CHO → CH₃COOH. Ethanal is only the intermediate, isolated with a mild oxidant such as Cu/O₂. Ethene and the ether come from dehydration, not oxidation.

questions.s: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CHO?
questions.e: The molecule has two carbons and an aldehyde group, –CHO, so it is ethanal (acetaldehyde). Ethanol, CH₃CH₂OH, ends in -ol, and methanal, HCHO, has only one carbon.

questions.s: Which class of compounds gives many fruits and flowers their pleasant smells?
questions.e: Low-molecular-mass esters such as ethyl ethanoate and 3-methylbutyl ethanoate (banana smell) are volatile and fruity-smelling. Carboxylic acids such as butanoic acid usually smell sharp or unpleasant, and alkanes and amino acids have little odour.

questions.s: Starch is completely hydrolysed by dilute acid or by enzymes. What is the final product?
questions.e: Starch is a polymer of glucose units: (C₆H₁₀O₅)ₙ + nH₂O → nC₆H₁₂O₆. Maltose is an intermediate, but complete hydrolysis gives only glucose. Fructose comes from sucrose, and glycerol from fats.

questions.s: Which functional group is present in butanone, CH₃COCH₂CH₃?
questions.e: The C=O group sits between two carbon atoms (CH₃– and –CH₂CH₃), which makes it a ketone. An aldehyde would have the C=O at the end of the chain with an H attached, and there is no –OH or –O– to make a carboxyl or ester group.

questions.s: Which of these is a natural polymer?
questions.e: Cellulose is made by plants from glucose units and forms cell walls, cotton and wood. Poly(ethene), nylon-6,6 and PVC are synthetic polymers made industrially from petrochemicals.

questions.s: A hydrocarbon is described as saturated when
o: it burns with a smoky flame
it is a gas at room temperature
it has only C–C single bonds
questions.e: Saturated means every carbon is bonded to four other atoms by single bonds, so no more hydrogen can be added; alkanes are saturated. A benzene ring and a smoky flame point to unsaturation (a high carbon content), and physical state has nothing to do with it.

questions.s: Structural isomers are compounds that have
o: the same element in different forms
questions.e: Isomers share a molecular formula but differ in how the atoms are connected, for example butane and 2-methylpropane, both C₄H₁₀. Formulas differing by CH₂ describe a homologous series, and different forms of one element are allotropes.

questions.s: Ethene reacts with steam at high temperature and pressure over a phosphoric acid catalyst. What is the product?
questions.e: Water adds across the C=C bond (hydration): CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O → CH₃CH₂OH. This is the main industrial route to ethanol. Ethane would need H₂, and ethanal and acetic acid are oxidation products, not addition products.

questions.s: 2 L of ethene burns completely in oxygen. What volume of oxygen is needed, measured at the same temperature and pressure?
questions.e: C₂H₄ + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 2H₂O, and for gases the volume ratio equals the mole ratio, so 2 × 3 = 6 L of O₂. 4 L is the volume of CO₂ formed, and 7 L would be the oxygen needed for ethane (3.5 per molecule).

questions.s: Methane and excess chlorine are mixed and left in diffuse light. How many different chlorine-containing organic products can form?
questions.e: Substitution continues step by step: CH₃Cl, CH₂Cl₂, CHCl₃ and CCl₄, so 4 organic products form (with HCl as the inorganic product). Answering 1 assumes the reaction stops after the first substitution, but every product still has H atoms (until CCl₄) that can be replaced.

questions.s: Which compound is an isomer of ethyl ethanoate, CH₃COOCH₂CH₃?
questions.e: Ethyl ethanoate is C₄H₈O₂, and butanoic acid, CH₃CH₂CH₂COOH, is also C₄H₈O₂, so they are functional-group isomers. Ethyl methanoate and propanoic acid are C₃H₆O₂, and butanal is C₄H₈O, with one oxygen fewer.

questions.s: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH=C(CH₃)CH₂CH₃?
questions.e: The longest chain containing the C=C has 5 carbons. Numbering from the left gives the double bond locant 2 (lower than 3 from the right) and puts the methyl on C3: 3-methylpent-2-ene. '2-ethylbut-2-ene' misses the five-carbon chain.

questions.s: Which compound reacts with sodium hydroxide solution?
questions.e: In phenol the O–H is attached to a benzene ring, which stabilises the phenoxide ion, so phenol is weakly acidic and forms sodium phenoxide with NaOH. Ordinary alcohols are much weaker acids than water, so they do not react with NaOH solution (they do react with sodium metal).

questions.s: Glucose in a urine sample is detected by heating it with freshly prepared Cu(OH)₂ in excess NaOH. What indicates a positive result?
questions.e: The aldehyde group of glucose reduces Cu(II) to brick-red Cu₂O. A silver mirror is the Tollens' result, blue-black is the iodine test for starch, and violet is the biuret test for proteins.

questions.s: 0.20 mol of acetic acid reacts completely with excess sodium hydrogencarbonate solution: CH₃COOH + NaHCO₃ → CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂. What volume of CO₂ is released at STP? (molar volume 22.4 L/mol)
questions.e: The equation is 1 : 1, so 0.20 mol of acid gives 0.20 mol of CO₂, and 0.20 × 22.4 = 4.48 L. 2.24 L would follow from the 2 : 1 ratio of the reaction with sodium carbonate, which does not apply to the hydrogencarbonate.

questions.s: A gaseous hydrocarbon has a density of 1.25 g/L at STP and decolourises bromine water. What is its formula? (H = 1, C = 12; molar volume 22.4 L/mol)
questions.e: M = 1.25 × 22.4 = 28 g/mol. The only formula with M = 28 is C₂H₄ (ethene), which is unsaturated and so decolourises bromine water. C₂H₂ (26) also decolourises it but has the wrong molar mass, and C₂H₆ (30) does not react.

questions.s: An organic compound contains 40.0% C, 6.7% H and 53.3% O by mass, has Mr = 60, and releases CO₂ from NaHCO₃ solution. What is it? (H = 1, C = 12, O = 16)
questions.e: Mole ratio C : H : O = 40.0/12 : 6.7/1 : 53.3/16 = 3.33 : 6.7 : 3.33 = 1 : 2 : 1, so the empirical formula is CH₂O; Mr 60 gives C₂H₄O₂. Methyl methanoate and HOCH₂CHO have the same formula but are not acidic, so only acetic acid reacts with NaHCO₃. Ethanol is C₂H₆O.

questions.s: How many carboxylic acids have the molecular formula C₅H₁₀O₂?
questions.e: The acid is C₄H₉–COOH, and there are four C₄H₉ groups: pentanoic acid, 2-methylbutanoic acid, 3-methylbutanoic acid and 2,2-dimethylpropanoic acid. So there are 4 acids; answering 2 counts only the unbranched and one branched chain.

questions.s: 4.4 g of a saturated ester with formula CₙH₂ₙO₂ reacts exactly with 50 mL of 1.0 mol/L NaOH solution. What is its molecular formula? (H = 1, C = 12, O = 16)
questions.e: n(NaOH) = 0.050 × 1.0 = 0.050 mol, and an ester with one –COO– group reacts 1 : 1, so Mr = 4.4/0.050 = 88. CₙH₂ₙO₂ has Mr = 14n + 32 = 88, giving n = 4: C₄H₈O₂. Using 50 instead of 0.050 L for the volume gives a nonsensical result.

questions.s: 2-bromobutane, CH₃CHBrCH₂CH₃, is heated with NaOH in ethanol. How many different alkenes can form if cis and trans isomers are counted separately?
questions.e: HBr can be removed with an H from C1, giving but-1-ene, or with an H from C3, giving but-2-ene, which exists as cis and trans forms. That makes 3 alkenes. Answering 2 forgets the geometric isomers of but-2-ene.

questions.s: In propene, CH₂=CHCH₃, what is the maximum number of atoms that can lie in the same plane?
questions.e: The C=C unit is planar, so both double-bond carbons, the three H atoms on them and the methyl carbon (6 atoms) are coplanar. The methyl carbon is tetrahedral, but rotation can bring one of its H atoms into that plane, giving 7. All 9 atoms cannot be coplanar because of the tetrahedral CH₃.

questions.s: Acrylic glass (PMMA) has the repeating unit –CH₂–C(CH₃)(COOCH₃)–. What is its monomer?
questions.e: For an addition polymer, restore the C=C between the two main-chain carbons and keep every side group: CH₂=C(CH₃)COOCH₃ (methyl 2-methylpropenoate). CH₃CH(CH₃)COOCH₃ has no double bond, CH₂=CHCOOCH₃ lacks the CH₃ side group, and CH₂=C(CH₃)COOH lacks the methyl ester group.

questions.s: The dipeptide H₂NCH₂CONHCH(CH₃)COOH is completely hydrolysed. What are the products?
questions.e: Hydrolysis breaks the peptide bond –CO–NH–: the C=O side gains –OH and the N–H side gains H, giving glycine H₂NCH₂COOH and alanine H₂NCH(CH₃)COOH. Breaking the bond elsewhere, as in the other options, would not restore two amino acids.

questions.s: What is the oxidation state of manganese in potassium permanganate, KMnO₄?
questions.e: K is +1 and each O is −2, so Mn + 1 − 8 = 0 gives Mn = +7. The value +6 belongs to manganate, K₂MnO₄, and +4 to MnO₂; both come from mixing up related manganese compounds.

questions.s: What is the oxidation state of sulfur in sulfurous acid, H₂SO₃?
questions.e: 2(+1) + S + 3(−2) = 0 gives S = +4. The value +6 is sulfur in sulfuric acid, H₂SO₄, which has one more oxygen atom; −2 is sulfur in H₂S.

questions.s: In which species does chromium have the oxidation state +6?
questions.e: In the dichromate ion, 2Cr + 7(−2) = −2, so 2Cr = +12 and Cr = +6. In Cr₂O₃, CrCl₃ and Cr(OH)₃ chromium is +3; a common slip is to forget the ion's −2 charge and get +7 for dichromate.

questions.s: Ammonium nitrate, NH₄NO₃, contains nitrogen in two different oxidation states. What are they?
questions.e: In NH₄⁺, N + 4(+1) = +1 gives N = −3; in NO₃⁻, N + 3(−2) = −1 gives N = +5. Treating the whole compound at once gives an average of +1 per nitrogen, which hides the two real states.

questions.s: What is the oxidation state of hydrogen in sodium hydride, NaH?
questions.e: Sodium is always +1 in its compounds, so hydrogen must be −1; NaH contains the hydride ion, H⁻. The usual value +1 applies when hydrogen is bonded to a more electronegative non-metal, as in H₂O or HCl, not to a reactive metal.

questions.s: In which compound does oxygen have a positive oxidation state?
questions.e: Fluorine is the most electronegative element and is always −1, so in OF₂ oxygen is +2. In the peroxides H₂O₂ and Na₂O₂ oxygen is −1 and in the superoxide KO₂ it is −½; these are unusual values but still negative.

questions.s: Magnetite, Fe₃O₄, can be written as FeO·Fe₂O₃. What is the ratio of iron(II) ions to iron(III) ions in Fe₃O₄?
questions.e: FeO supplies one Fe²⁺ and Fe₂O₃ supplies two Fe³⁺, so the ratio is 1:2. Check: 2 + 2 × 3 = 8 = 4 × 2, matching four O²⁻. The average oxidation state is +8/3, but that is not a ratio of ions.

questions.s: In which compound does carbon have the oxidation state 0?
questions.e: In methanal, CH₂O, 2(+1) + C + (−2) = 0 gives C = 0. Carbon is +2 in CO, −4 in CH₄ and +4 in CO₂; a compound of carbon can still have carbon at oxidation state 0.

questions.s: In which compound does chlorine have the oxidation state +5?
questions.e: In KClO₃, +1 + Cl + 3(−2) = 0 gives Cl = +5. Chlorine is +1 in HClO, +3 in HClO₂ and +7 in HClO₄, rising by 2 for each extra oxygen atom.

questions.s: Which statement describes oxidation?
questions.e: Oxidation is loss of electrons, which raises the oxidation state. Gain of electrons, a decrease in oxidation state and gain of hydrogen all describe reduction.

questions.s: Which of the following is a redox reaction?
questions.e: Zinc goes from 0 to +2 and copper from +2 to 0, so electrons are transferred. In the decomposition of CaCO₃, the neutralisation and the precipitation of AgCl, no element changes its oxidation state.

questions.s: In the reaction Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu, which species is the oxidising agent?
questions.e: Cu²⁺ gains two electrons and is reduced to Cu, so it is the oxidising agent. Zinc loses electrons and is the reducing agent; a common mistake is to call the substance that is oxidised the oxidising agent.

questions.s: For the reaction 2Na + Cl₂ → 2NaCl, which statement is correct?
o: Each sodium atom loses one electron
Each chlorine atom loses one electron
questions.e: Na goes from 0 to +1 by losing one electron, and each Cl atom gains one electron to become Cl⁻. So sodium is oxidised (it is the reducing agent) and chlorine is the oxidising agent.

questions.s: Which change needs an oxidising agent to make it happen?
questions.e: Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺ raises the oxidation state from +2 to +3, so electrons must be removed by an oxidising agent. Cl₂ → Cl⁻ and MnO₄⁻ → Mn²⁺ are reductions, and in SO₃ → H₂SO₄ sulfur stays at +6, so only water is needed.

questions.s: Which conversion requires a reducing agent?
questions.e: In CuO → Cu, copper falls from +2 to 0, which is reduction and needs a reducing agent such as H₂ or CO. The other three changes raise an oxidation state (Fe 0 → +2, C +2 → +4, I −1 → 0), so they need oxidising agents.

questions.s: Considering only the oxidation state of sulfur, which species can act both as an oxidising agent and as a reducing agent?
questions.e: Sulfur in SO₂ is +4, between its lowest state (−2) and highest state (+6), so it can be either reduced or oxidised. In H₂S and Na₂S sulfur is already −2, so it can only be oxidised; in H₂SO₄ it is +6 and can only be reduced.

questions.s: Which particle can act only as an oxidising agent?
questions.e: Aluminium has no oxidation state above +3, so Al³⁺ can only gain electrons and act as an oxidising agent. Na metal can only lose electrons, and Fe²⁺ and S are in intermediate states, so they can act either way.

questions.s: Chlorine is made in the laboratory by heating MnO₂ with concentrated hydrochloric acid: MnO₂ + 4HCl → MnCl₂ + Cl₂ + 2H₂O. What fraction of the HCl acts as a reducing agent?
questions.e: Of the four Cl⁻, two are oxidised to Cl₂ and two remain as Cl⁻ in MnCl₂, so 2/4 = 1/2 of the HCl is the reducing agent. The other half only acts as an acid, so assuming all the HCl is oxidised is the trap.

questions.s: Copper reacts with dilute nitric acid: 3Cu + 8HNO₃ → 3Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2NO + 4H₂O. When 0.3 mol Cu reacts completely, how many moles of HNO₃ are reduced?
questions.e: 3 mol Cu gives 2 mol NO, so 0.3 mol Cu gives 0.2 mol NO, and each NO comes from one reduced HNO₃ (N +5 → +2). Electron check: 0.3 × 2 = 0.6 mol lost and 0.2 × 3 = 0.6 mol gained. 0.8 mol is the total HNO₃ used; 0.6 mol of it only forms the nitrate salt.

questions.s: Potassium chlorate decomposes on heating with a MnO₂ catalyst: 2KClO₃ → 2KCl + 3O₂. How many moles of electrons are transferred when 3 mol O₂ is produced?
questions.e: Each Cl goes from +5 to −1, gaining 6 electrons, so 2 mol KClO₃ gains 12 mol electrons. Check with oxygen: 6 mol O atoms go from −2 to 0, losing 12 mol electrons. 6 mol counts only one KClO₃.

questions.s: Hydrogen peroxide decomposes: 2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂. How many moles of electrons are transferred for each 1 mol of O₂ formed?
questions.e: Oxygen in H₂O₂ is −1; the two O atoms that form O₂ each rise to 0, losing 2 electrons in total, while two others fall to −2. So 2 mol electrons per mol O₂. 4 mol would apply if the oxygen started at −2, as in the electrolysis of water.

questions.s: Chlorine reacts with cold sodium hydroxide solution: Cl₂ + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaClO + H₂O. Which statement is correct?
o: Cl₂ is the oxidising agent only
NaOH is the reducing agent here
Cl₂ is both oxidised and reduced
questions.e: One Cl atom goes from 0 to −1 (in NaCl) and the other from 0 to +1 (in NaClO), so chlorine disproportionates. Only one electron passes per Cl₂, and Na, O and H keep their oxidation states, so NaOH is neither oxidised nor reduced.

questions.s: In a blast furnace, Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂. How many moles of electrons are transferred when 1 mol Fe₂O₃ is reduced to iron?
questions.e: Each Fe goes from +3 to 0, gaining 3 electrons, and there are two Fe per Fe₂O₃, so 6 mol. Check: 3 mol CO each lose 2 electrons (C +2 → +4), also 6 mol. 3 mol forgets the second iron atom.

questions.s: Which statement about redox reactions is correct?
o: The oxidising agent is itself reduced
Every combination reaction is a redox reaction
questions.e: The oxidising agent takes electrons from another substance, so it is reduced. Oxidation and reduction always happen together, a reducing agent loses electrons, and combinations such as CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ involve no change of oxidation state.

questions.s: Both of these reactions take place in solution: 2Fe³⁺ + 2I⁻ → 2Fe²⁺ + I₂ and Br₂ + 2Fe²⁺ → 2Fe³⁺ + 2Br⁻. Which order of oxidising strength is correct?
questions.e: In a reaction that occurs, the oxidising agent is stronger than the oxidised product. The first reaction gives Fe³⁺ > I₂ and the second gives Br₂ > Fe³⁺, so Br₂ > Fe³⁺ > I₂. Reversing the rule gives the order I₂ > Fe³⁺ > Br₂.

questions.s: When the equation MnO₄⁻ + Fe²⁺ + H⁺ → Mn²⁺ + Fe³⁺ + H₂O is balanced with the smallest whole numbers, what is the coefficient of Fe²⁺?
questions.e: Mn falls from +7 to +2, gaining 5 electrons, and each Fe²⁺ loses 1, so 5Fe²⁺ are needed per MnO₄⁻. The full equation is MnO₄⁻ + 5Fe²⁺ + 8H⁺ → Mn²⁺ + 5Fe³⁺ + 4H₂O, with charge +17 on each side. The 8 is the coefficient of H⁺, not Fe²⁺.

questions.s: Acidified permanganate oxidises hydrogen peroxide: 2MnO₄⁻ + aH₂O₂ + bH⁺ → 2Mn²⁺ + cO₂ + dH₂O. What are the values of a and b?
questions.e: Two Mn gain 2 × 5 = 10 electrons; each H₂O₂ loses 2 (O −1 → 0), so a = 5 and c = 5. Charge: −2 + b = +4 gives b = 6, and then H gives d = 8 (10 + 6 = 16). The pair a = 5, b = 8 comes from copying the 8H⁺ of the iron(II) equation.

questions.s: In the catalytic oxidation of ammonia, NH₃ + O₂ → NO + H₂O. When the equation is balanced with the smallest whole numbers, what is the sum of all the coefficients?
questions.e: N goes from −3 to +2 (loses 5) and each O₂ gains 4, so 4NH₃ react with 5O₂: 4NH₃ + 5O₂ → 4NO + 6H₂O. The sum is 4 + 5 + 4 + 6 = 19. Balancing hydrogen first with 2NH₃ leads to fractional O₂ and errors.

questions.s: Copper reacts with concentrated nitric acid: Cu + aHNO₃ → Cu(NO₃)₂ + bNO₂ + cH₂O. What is the value of a?
questions.e: Cu loses 2 electrons and each N going to NO₂ (+5 → +4) gains 1, so b = 2. Two more HNO₃ supply the nitrate in Cu(NO₃)₂, giving a = 4 and c = 2. Answering 2 counts only the nitric acid that is reduced.

questions.s: Hot concentrated sulfuric acid oxidises carbon: C + 2H₂SO₄ → CO₂ + 2SO₂ + 2H₂O. What is the mole ratio of oxidising agent to reducing agent?
questions.e: Carbon (0 → +4) is the reducing agent and loses 4 electrons; each H₂SO₄ that becomes SO₂ (+6 → +4) gains 2, so 2 mol H₂SO₄ oxidise 1 mol C. Here all the acid is reduced, so the ratio is 2:1; reversing the roles gives 1:2.

questions.s: Potassium permanganate reacts with concentrated hydrochloric acid: 2KMnO₄ + 16HCl → 2KCl + 2MnCl₂ + 5Cl₂ + 8H₂O. What is the mole ratio of KMnO₄ to the HCl that is actually oxidised?
questions.e: 5 mol Cl₂ contain 10 mol Cl atoms, so 10 of the 16 HCl are oxidised; the other 6 end up as Cl⁻ in KCl and MnCl₂. The ratio is 2:10 = 1:5, which also matches 2 × 5 electrons gained = 10 × 1 electrons lost. 1:8 uses all 16 HCl.

questions.s: Nitrogen dioxide reacts with water: 3NO₂ + H₂O → 2HNO₃ + NO. What is the mass ratio of NO₂ reduced to NO₂ oxidised?
questions.e: Two N atoms rise from +4 to +5 (oxidised, forming HNO₃) and one falls from +4 to +2 (reduced, forming NO). Since it is the same substance, the mass ratio equals the mole ratio, reduced : oxidised = 1:2. The answer 2:1 gives the ratio the wrong way round.

questions.s: Chlorine reacts with hot potassium hydroxide solution: 3Cl₂ + 6KOH → 5KCl + KClO₃ + 3H₂O. How many moles of electrons are transferred when 3 mol Cl₂ reacts?
questions.e: Of the six Cl atoms, one rises from 0 to +5 in KClO₃, losing 5 electrons, and five fall from 0 to −1 in KCl, gaining 5 in total. So 5 mol electrons are transferred. Counting one electron for every Cl atom gives the wrong value 6 mol.

questions.s: Hydrogen sulfide reacts with sulfur dioxide: 2H₂S + SO₂ → 3S + 2H₂O. What is the mass ratio of the sulfur formed by oxidation to the sulfur formed by reduction?
questions.e: Two S atoms from H₂S rise from −2 to 0 (oxidation) and one S atom from SO₂ falls from +4 to 0 (reduction). All three are sulfur atoms of equal mass, so the ratio is 2:1. Mixing up which reactant is oxidised gives 1:2.

questions.s: Potassium chlorate reacts with concentrated hydrochloric acid: KClO₃ + 6HCl → KCl + 3Cl₂ + 3H₂O. What is the ratio of chlorine atoms oxidised to chlorine atoms reduced?
questions.e: The Cl in KClO₃ goes from +5 to 0 (one atom reduced, gaining 5 electrons), and five Cl⁻ from HCl go from −1 to 0 (oxidised, losing 5 in total). The sixth Cl⁻ simply ends up in KCl. So the ratio is 5:1; 6:1 wrongly counts all the HCl as oxidised.

questions.s: An acidified solution containing 0.5 mol Fe²⁺ is oxidised completely to Fe³⁺ by KMnO₄, which is reduced to Mn²⁺. How many moles of KMnO₄ are needed?
questions.e: 0.5 mol Fe²⁺ loses 0.5 mol electrons. Each MnO₄⁻ gains 5 electrons (+7 → +2), so 0.5/5 = 0.1 mol KMnO₄ is needed. 2.5 mol comes from multiplying by 5 instead of dividing.

questions.s: 24 mL of 0.05 mol/L Na₂SO₃ solution exactly reduces 20 mL of 0.02 mol/L K₂Cr₂O₇ solution, and the sulfite is oxidised to sulfate. What is the oxidation state of chromium in the product?
questions.e: Sulfite: 0.024 × 0.05 = 0.0012 mol, each losing 2 electrons (S +4 → +6), so 0.0024 mol electrons. Dichromate: 0.020 × 0.02 = 0.0004 mol, containing 0.0008 mol Cr, so each Cr gains 0.0024/0.0008 = 3 electrons and falls from +6 to +3. Forgetting that each ion contains two Cr atoms would give an impossible 6 electrons per Cr.

questions.s: The order of reducing power is I⁻ > Fe²⁺ > Br⁻ > Cl⁻. Which reaction cannot take place?
questions.e: A reaction occurs only if the reducing agent is stronger than the reduced product. In I₂ + 2Fe²⁺ → 2Fe³⁺ + 2I⁻ the reducing agent Fe²⁺ would have to be stronger than I⁻, which contradicts the order. In each of the other reactions the reducing agent (I⁻, Br⁻, Fe²⁺) is stronger than its product.

questions.s: 0.1 mol Cl₂ is passed into a solution containing 0.1 mol FeBr₂. The reducing power of Fe²⁺ is greater than that of Br⁻. What fraction of the Br⁻ ions is oxidised?
questions.e: Fe²⁺ reacts first: 0.1 mol Fe²⁺ uses 0.05 mol Cl₂ (2Fe²⁺ + Cl₂ → 2Fe³⁺ + 2Cl⁻). The remaining 0.05 mol Cl₂ oxidises 0.1 mol Br⁻ (Cl₂ + 2Br⁻ → Br₂ + 2Cl⁻), which is half of the 0.2 mol Br⁻ present. Answering none assumes Cl₂ runs out on Fe²⁺.

questions.s: Iron powder is added slowly to a solution containing both AgNO₃ and Cu(NO₃)₂. Which statement describes what happens?
o: Both ions are reduced at once
questions.e: Silver is less reactive than copper, so Ag⁺ is the stronger oxidising agent and takes electrons from iron first: Fe + 2Ag⁺ → Fe²⁺ + 2Ag. Only after the Ag⁺ is used up does Cu²⁺ react. Iron is more reactive than both metals, so it does react.

questions.s: Metals X, Y and Z all form 2+ ions. X reacts with a solution of Y²⁺ to give Y; Z reacts with Y²⁺ to give Y; Z does not react with a solution of X²⁺. What is the order of reducing power?
questions.e: A metal displaces another only if it is the stronger reducing agent. X > Y and Z > Y from the first two results, and Z does not displace X, so X > Z. Together X > Z > Y; Z > X > Y ignores the failed reaction.

questions.s: In a galvanic (voltaic) cell, which statement is correct?
o: Electrical energy is converted into chemical energy
Oxidation takes place at the negative electrode
Cations move towards the negative electrode
questions.e: The negative electrode releases electrons into the external circuit, so oxidation happens there. A galvanic cell turns chemical energy into electrical energy, electrons travel through the wire (not the solution), and cations move towards the positive electrode.

questions.s: A zinc strip and a copper strip are dipped into dilute sulfuric acid and joined by a wire. What is observed at the copper strip?
questions.e: Zinc is the negative electrode and is oxidised; the electrons flow through the wire to copper, where 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂. Copper itself is not attacked, and no Cu²⁺ is present to deposit copper.

questions.s: A cell consists of a zinc rod in ZnSO₄ solution and a copper rod in CuSO₄ solution, connected by a wire and by a salt bridge containing KCl. Which statement is correct while the cell works?
o: Electrons flow from copper to zinc
K⁺ ions move into the ZnSO₄ solution
Cl⁻ ions move into the ZnSO₄ solution
questions.e: Zinc is oxidised, so Zn²⁺ builds up in its half-cell and Cl⁻ from the salt bridge moves in to balance the charge; K⁺ moves the other way, into the CuSO₄ solution. Electrons flow from zinc to copper, and copper is deposited, so the copper rod gets heavier.

questions.s: An iron rod and a copper rod are joined by a wire and dipped into CuSO₄ solution. What is the reaction at the positive electrode?
questions.e: Iron is more reactive, so it is the negative electrode and is oxidised to Fe²⁺. Electrons flow to the copper rod, where Cu²⁺ ions from the solution are reduced to copper. The equation Fe → Fe²⁺ + 2e⁻ is the negative-electrode reaction, and iron does not form Fe³⁺ here.

questions.s: A magnesium strip and an aluminium strip, joined by a wire, are dipped into sodium hydroxide solution. Which is the negative electrode, and why?
o: Mg, as magnesium is the more reactive metal
Al, as only aluminium reacts with NaOH(aq)
Mg, as only magnesium reacts with NaOH(aq)
Al, as aluminium is the less reactive metal
