questions.e: CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂ gives a steady, easily controlled stream of gas. With sulfuric acid, slightly soluble CaSO₄ coats the marble and the reaction stops; powdered Na₂CO₃ with concentrated acid reacts too fast to control, and limestone needs about 900 °C to decompose.

questions.s: Where should your eye be when reading the volume of water in a measuring cylinder?
o: Level with the edge of the meniscus where it touches the glass
Level with the bottom of the meniscus
questions.e: Water forms a concave meniscus, and the volume is read at its lowest point with the eye level with it. Looking from above makes the reading too high, and looking from below makes it too low (parallax error).

questions.s: Which reagent distinguishes dilute hydrochloric acid from dilute sulfuric acid?
questions.e: Ba²⁺ + SO₄²⁻ → BaSO₄, a white precipitate, forms only with sulfuric acid. Both acids turn litmus red, give hydrogen with zinc and give CO₂ with sodium carbonate, so those reagents give the same result for both.

questions.s: Which set of raw materials is fed into a blast furnace to make iron?
o: Iron ore, coke, limestone and hot air
questions.e: Coke burns in the hot air to give heat and carbon monoxide (the reducing agent), and limestone removes sandy impurities as slag. Cryolite is used in aluminium extraction, and sand is the impurity to be removed, not a raw material.

questions.s: Which statement about the iron catalyst in the Haber process is correct?
o: It increases the equilibrium yield of ammonia
It shifts the equilibrium to the right
It lets equilibrium be reached faster without changing the yield
It is used up and must be replaced after each batch
questions.e: A catalyst lowers the activation energy of both the forward and reverse reactions equally, so equilibrium is reached faster but its position, and the yield, are unchanged. A catalyst is not consumed in the reaction.

questions.s: What is the safe way to smell a gas in the laboratory?
o: Put your nose over the mouth of the container and breathe in deeply
Pour a little gas onto your hand and sniff your hand
Smell it only after heating the container
Waft a little gas towards your nose with your hand
questions.e: Gently wafting brings only a small amount of gas to the nose, so a toxic or irritating gas cannot cause serious harm. Breathing in deeply over the container could deliver a dangerous dose.

questions.s: Crude rock salt contains sand. In which order should the operations be done to obtain clean salt?
o: Dissolve in water, filter, evaporate the filtrate
questions.e: Dissolving puts the salt into solution, filtering removes the insoluble sand, and evaporating the filtrate gives salt crystals. Evaporating before filtering would leave the sand mixed with the salt again.

questions.s: Which drying agent can be used to dry chlorine?
questions.e: Chlorine is an acidic gas, so it must be dried with an acidic or neutral drying agent; concentrated H₂SO₄ does not react with it. Soda lime, solid NaOH and CaO are basic and react with chlorine (for example Cl₂ + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaClO + H₂O).

questions.s: In the electrolytic refining of copper, which arrangement is correct?
o: Pure copper anode, impure copper cathode, CuSO₄ solution
Impure copper anode, pure copper cathode, NaCl solution
Graphite anode, pure copper cathode, CuSO₄ solution
Impure copper anode, pure copper cathode, CuSO₄ solution
questions.e: Copper from the impure anode dissolves as Cu²⁺ and pure copper is deposited on the cathode from the CuSO₄ electrolyte. Swapping the electrodes would dissolve the pure copper, and a graphite anode would release oxygen instead of dissolving the impure copper, so nothing would be refined.

questions.s: A sodium chloride solution contains a little sodium carbonate. Which reagent removes the carbonate without adding a new impurity?
o: An appropriate amount of dilute hydrochloric acid
questions.e: Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂, so the carbonate becomes the wanted NaCl and the CO₂ escapes. Sulfuric and nitric acids would leave Na₂SO₄ or NaNO₃ as new impurities, and NaOH does not react with Na₂CO₃.

questions.s: In the Haber process, which choice is made mainly to increase the rate rather than the equilibrium yield?
o: Using an iron catalyst and a temperature of about 450 °C
Recycling the unreacted nitrogen and hydrogen
questions.e: The catalyst and the fairly high temperature speed up the reaction; the temperature actually lowers the equilibrium yield, and the catalyst does not change it. High pressure raises both rate and yield, while removing ammonia and recycling gases improve the overall conversion.
